title: OPERATION FIRST INSULT
skeleton: raider must inflict precisely calibrated, attributable damage on a producing site - enough to demand an answer, too little to be an atrocity - while overkill is permanently available and self-defeating
inspiration: the Doolittle Raid, 1942 (a strike whose strategic value was the message it sent, not the damage it did)
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} border, {YEAR}. {EMPLOYER} has ordered one careful strike against {TARGET_FACTION}'s heavy foundry in the industrial belt. The goal is not to destroy the production line. It is to visibly cripple it, so the district's commander must strike back or lose face with his own superiors. This is the first move in a planned feud: a raid meant to be survived, traced to {EMPLOYER}, and resented. The foundry sits at the head of the rail cut, a 6-kilometer trench dug to carry ore from the open pits to the smelters. The cut is the terrain problem. It is 90 meters wide at the floor and walled by 40-meter rock faces on both sides. It is the only path a 'Mech can take to the foundry gantries without crossing the open pit lakes, so it is also where the defender expects you. {NPC:intel-source} reports the foundry keeps a security section: one reinforced 'Mech lance plus a tracked-armor platoon, Regular quality, with dug-in Goblin emplacements covering the trench floor. That report is 11 days old, so treat the numbers as a floor, not a ceiling. The pour schedule matters. At shift change, 0600 and 1800 local, the gantry cranes lift 60-ton crucibles of molten metal over the casting floor. If a crucible is hit during a firefight, it drops and guts the line for a year. That would turn a measured insult into a war crime {EMPLOYER} cannot be seen to commit. Your job is to break the rolling mill and the No. 2 furnace tap, both repairable in 90 to 120 days, then withdraw with the damage clearly the work of an outside lance. Leave the crucibles alone. The foundry is worth more standing, so the enemy has something to defend next time. In the cut, the rock walls blind magscan past 300 meters and trap engine heat. A 'Mech that has moved through leaves a warm heat trace on the trench floor for 4 to 6 minutes. The gunners can mistake that fading trace for a live target. About 800 foundry workers are on shift at any hour, housed in barracks 1.2 kilometers from the casting floor. They will not fight. They will photograph everything, and the images will reach the district commander's staff within a day. That is the point. This raid is meant to be seen.

objectives.primary: Disable the No. 2 furnace tap and the rolling mill drive train — damage rated at 90 days' minimum repair, both confirmed wrecked before withdrawal.
objectives.secondary: Withdraw the full raiding force off-world with no unit captured and no machine left identifiable to {EMPLOYER}.
objectives.bonus: Leave the casting floor and its loaded crucibles untouched. The strike then reads as professional restraint, not terror, and the district commander is more likely to answer it out of pride.

complications.name: The Pour Schedule
complications.text: At 0600 and 1800 the gantry cranes lift loaded crucibles over the casting floor. A stray hit on a gantry during these windows drops 60 tons of molten metal across the shop, killing workers and gutting the line for a year. {EMPLOYER}'s feud needs a lamed foundry, not a slaughtered one.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If any weapons fire hits a gantry hex during a pour window, the bonus objective is voided and a permanent employer-standing penalty applies. The line is destroyed instead of disabled, and the reprisal fork escalates one threat tier.

complications.name: Trench Heat Traces
complications.text: The rock walls of the cut trap engine heat. A 'Mech that moves through leaves a warm heat trace on the trench floor for 4 to 6 minutes after it has gone. The defender's gunners can mistake that fading trace for a live target, so the ground draws fire onto spots your machines have already left.
complications.mechanicalEffect: After any friendly 'Mech leaves a trench-floor hex, that hex reads as a thermal contact to the defender for the next 2 turns. The defender may make one indirect-fire attack per turn against such a hex.

complications.name: Eight Hundred Witnesses
complications.text: Foundry workers will photograph the raid from the barracks blocks. That imagery is how the strike gets traced to {EMPLOYER}, which is the whole point. But a single civilian death in the frame turns a survivable insult into an atrocity, and the enemy answers an atrocity with a punitive war, not a measured reprisal.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any collateral damage to the barracks blocks or worker casualties converts the FULL_SUCCESS and SUCCESS forks' typed follow-on to the COMPROMISED branch regardless of objective completion.

decisionPoints.name: Reaching the Foundry
decisionPoints.context: The rail cut is the obvious road and the defender knows it. The pit-lake causeways are slower, wetter, and partially flooded, but they bypass the trench emplacements. How you arrive decides whether you fight the Goblins on their ground or your own.

options.title: Drive the Cut
advantages: Direct line to the gantries — fastest demolition setup
Rock walls protect your flanks from the armor platoon's wider envelopment
disadvantages: The Goblin emplacements have ranged the trench floor for years
Thermal ghosts let the defender place fire where you have just been
options.consequence: You trade time for a head-on fight against prepared positions; demolition begins early but under direct fire from the trench guns.

costs.resource: ammunition: a head-on breach burns the SRM and short-range load you brought for the demolition fight
costs.risk: The trench guns have pre-ranged the floor — the first two turns are fought inside their cone whether you like it or not

options.title: Cross the Pit-Lake Causeways
advantages: Bypasses the trench emplacements entirely
Arrives on the foundry's flank, away from the prepared kill zone
disadvantages: Flooded causeway sections limit 'Mechs to 50 tons and below at safe footing
Slower approach concedes time the defender uses to reposition armor
options.consequence: You arrive unblooded but late, against a defender who has had time to wheel his armor onto the casting-floor approaches.

costs.resource: time: the causeway crossing adds two turns of movement before contact
costs.risk: Weight ceiling forces your heaviest 'Mech to take the Cut alone or stay home

options.title: Demolition Charge the Trench Wall
advantages: A blown rock face creates a new entry the defender has not ranged
Collapses one Goblin emplacement under rubble before the fight begins
disadvantages: Charge placement requires a dismounted tech team and a 40-minute fuse window
The blast announces the raid before the demolition objective is even started
options.consequence: You buy a fresh approach at the price of surprise; the defender's reaction clock starts at the wall blast, not at the foundry gate.

costs.resource: demolition stores: shaped charges and a dismounted tech team exposed for 40 minutes
costs.risk: A premature detonation or a discovered tech team starts the reaction timeline early with your force still strung out on the approach

entries.event: Foundry security control logs an unidentified 'Mech contact at the Cut mouth or the causeway flank; site alarm sounds and the security lance starts engines.
Goblin emplacements go weapons-free on the trench floor; the tracked-armor platoon moves to the casting-floor approaches.
Demolition of the furnace tap and rolling mill must be underway by now to finish inside the window; foundry workers begin evacuating the barracks blocks toward the imagery you want them to take.
District QRF lance, scrambled from the district garrison 22 kilometers off, reaches the foundry perimeter road.
QRF and the recovered security lance can fight as a combined force; your withdrawal window closes against superior numbers.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Both targets must be wrecked and the force moving to extraction by T+18:00. Miss it and the arriving QRF lance pins you against the foundry with the security section still fighting, and the raid fails because you are trapped, not because you did too little damage.

opforSketch.composition: One reinforced security lance of medium 'Mechs (40-60 tons) at Regular quality, defending a fixed site, supported by a tracked-armor platoon of 4 to 6 vehicles (Vedette/Goblin behavior) and 2 dug-in Goblin emplacements covering the trench floor. The emplaced vehicles do not maneuver; the platoon does. Heavy reliance on prepared positions and pre-ranged fire.
opforSketch.behavior: Site-defense doctrine: hold the trench guns as an anvil, maneuver the armor platoon to fix the raiders against the prepared kill zone, and protect the casting floor above all. The security lance fights conservatively to preserve the line; it breaks contact at 45 percent force damage and falls back to the gantry core rather than pursue.

forks.name: OPERATION RETURNED FAVOR
forks.trigger: Foundry lamed cleanly, force extracted, the strike attributed to {EMPLOYER} as intended.
forks.consequence: The district commander cannot let the insult stand. Within the season he stages a heavier reprisal against {EMPLOYER}'s own holdings — a stiffer raid your command must now garrison against, the feud's first answer.

forks.name: OPERATION COLD FORGE
forks.trigger: Foundry lamed, force extracted clean, AND the casting floor left untouched — the restraint reads as professionalism.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER}'s intelligence staff exploits the clean attribution to bait the district commander into a poorly chosen counter-raid that exposes a forward depot — a follow-on objective raid against a target the enemy revealed in his anger.

forks.name: OPERATION SPILLED CRUCIBLE
forks.trigger: Raid fails, a unit is captured, or the casting floor is destroyed and workers killed.
forks.consequence: The atrocity — real or pinned on you — gives the district commander moral cover for a punitive expedition. {EMPLOYER} pulls your command into a hasty defense of a settlement marked for reprisal, the feud now ugly and public.

storyElementSeed: A demolition tech kneels at the furnace tap, charge timer in hand, watching the gantry crane swing a loaded crucible across the far end of the shop. She counts the seconds until the metal is clear before she arms the fuse, because the order was to cripple the line, not kill the workers.

is-kurita.objectives.primary: The damage itself is the message. Break the No. 2 tap and the rolling mill precisely, and spare the casting floor on purpose. {EMPLOYER} requires that the district commander read the restraint as clearly as the insult.

merc.objectives.primary: Contract specifies disabling damage only — the auditors will assess repair time, and a destroyed line voids the restraint bonus in Section 9. Crucible damage triggers the atrocity-liability clause; read it before you commit a heavy 'Mech to the gantry approaches.

REPAIR_DAYS.unit: days to repair the disabled line

GHOST_PERSIST_MINUTES.unit: minutes a thermal ghost persists in the Cut

QRF_DISTANCE_KM.unit: kilometers to the district QRF garrison

phases.name: INGRESS — THE CUT MOUTH
phases.lead: The raid lives or dies on how it reaches the gantries. The rail cut is the fast road and the expected one; the causeways are slow and wet. The force commits to an approach before the first emplacement opens fire.

dataBlock.Cut dimensions: 90m wide at the floor, 40m rock walls, 6km from mouth to foundry gate
dataBlock.Causeway ceiling: Flooded sections rated to 50 tons safe footing; heavier machines must take the Cut
dataBlock.Sensor floor: Magscan blind under 300m in the trench; thermal returns bloom and persist 4-6 minutes
dataBlock.Pour windows: 0600 and 1800 local — loaded crucibles over the casting floor, no fire permitted near the gantries

routes.name: RED — THE CUT FLOOR
routes.desc: Direct down the trench to the foundry gate
routes.tradeoff: Fastest to the gantries; fought inside the pre-ranged trench-gun cone from the first turn

routes.name: BLUE — PIT-LAKE CAUSEWAYS
routes.desc: Flanking crossing over the flooded ore-pit causeways
routes.tradeoff: Bypasses the emplacements but caps 'Mech weight at 50 tons and costs two turns of approach

phases.protocol: Attribution is the mission: the raiding force shows a clean false unit blazon and uses no employer call-signs on any net. Codeword DROP CLEAR, passed on the demolition channel, means the gantry pour window has closed and weapons are free near the casting floor; until DROP CLEAR no fire is authorized within 200m of a loaded gantry.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Why a raid meant to be attributed is harder than one meant to vanish — the deliberate evidence trail you leave, and the single frame of a dead worker that would turn the whole message into a confession.

phases.name: GROUND — THE TAP AND THE MILL
phases.lead: Two targets, both repairable, both meant to read as the work of a professional outside lance. The demolition fight is short and loud; the discipline is in stopping there.

dataBlock.Primary charges: No. 2 furnace tap and the rolling-mill drive train — 90 to 120 day repair if cleanly broken
dataBlock.Forbidden targets: Loaded crucibles, gantry cranes, barracks blocks — any hit voids restraint and escalates the answer
dataBlock.Demolition window: Both targets wrecked and force moving by T+18:00 before the QRF closes
dataBlock.Thermal discipline: Every vacated trench hex reads as a live contact for 2 turns — do not loiter where you have stood

sidebarKernel.kernel: The difference between disabling a furnace tap and destroying it: where the charge goes for a 90-day repair versus a year, and why the easier shot is the wrong one here.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — BEFORE THE QRF
phases.lead: The security lance falls back to the gantry core; the district QRF is 18 to 26 kilometers out. The force withdraws the way it can, not the way it came, and clears the system before attribution turns into pursuit.

dataBlock.QRF arrival: T+18:00 to the perimeter road; combined enemy force fightable at T+26:00
dataBlock.Withdrawal ceiling: Causeway exit caps at 50 tons; the Cut exit risks the thermal-ghost gauntlet again
dataBlock.Off-world clock: Force clear of the foundry by T+18:00 to make the DropShip lift window

sidebarKernel.kernel: Why you withdraw before the QRF arrives even with the fight going your way — the feud needs the enemy alive and angry, not destroyed and avenged.

title: OPERATION ANSWERED HONOR
skeleton: defender must answer an enemy who arrives openly to collect an honor debt, choosing whether to win on the challenger's terms or favorable terrain while a self-imposed ban on its own heavy assets makes a dishonorable victory worse than defeat
inspiration: the medieval trial by combat / judicial duel (a challenge that must be answered in form, where winning by the wrong means loses the cause)
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} border, {YEAR}. Three months ago a {TARGET_FACTION} raid burned the regimental colors of the unit your command now reinforces. The district has not forgiven it, and the enemy commander, {NPC:opfor-commander}, is not finished. {NPC:intel-source} judges that the same officer means to return openly and challenge the garrison to a stand-up 'Mech fight on the open steppe, not another raid. He is coming to collect an honor debt in full view. That report is 8 days old and rated reliable. The terrain problem is the steppe itself: 200 kilometers of frozen high grassland with one feature that matters, a 9-kilometer cliff line that splits it into an upper and a lower shelf. The only vehicle route between the shelves is the switchback cut, a road 14 meters wide that a single lance can hold against a regiment. Whoever holds the cut decides where the duel happens. {EMPLOYER}, the district warlord, has set the political terms plainly. This is a matter of face, fought 'Mech against 'Mech under the old conventions. A garrison that hides behind fortifications or fields tanks against a 'Mech challenge will be remembered as having shamed the district a second time. You command the steppe garrison: your lance, plus a depleted house company of 8 'Mechs at Regular quality, still recovering from the raid that cost them their colors, billeted at the upper-shelf fort. The fort's fixed defenses work, but the warlord has forbidden their use against an honor challenge. Your operations officer has asked twice and been refused twice. The steppe is open and flat, with clear-day observation out to 8 kilometers. But ground blizzards roll off the cliff 5 days in 7 and cut visibility below 600 meters with no warning. Few civilians live here: nomadic herders who move 40,000 head of cattle along the lower shelf and will report the enemy's approach in exchange for being left to graze. The enemy is coming to be answered. The one thing the brief cannot decide for you is whether you answer him on his terms or on yours.

objectives.primary: Defeat or repulse {NPC:opfor-commander}'s reprisal force, holding the steppe garrison area and the upper-shelf fort against capture.
objectives.secondary: Conduct the engagement within the honor conventions the warlord has imposed — no fixed-defense fires, no non-'Mech combat units committed — so the district's face is restored, not further damaged.
objectives.bonus: Defeat {NPC:opfor-commander} in a way that breaks his unit's will to return — a decisive result that ends the cycle rather than feeding it.

complications.name: The Warlord's Constraint
complications.text: {EMPLOYER} has forbidden the use of the fort's fixed defenses and any non-'Mech combat unit against an honor challenge. The constraint is political, absolute, and twice-confirmed. Winning dishonorably loses the campaign even if it wins the battle.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If fixed-emplacement fire or any vehicle/aerospace unit engages the enemy 'Mech force, the secondary objective fails permanently and the district-standing reward is forfeit regardless of the battle's outcome.

complications.name: Escarpment Ground Blizzards
complications.text: Blizzards roll off the escarpment 5 days in 7 and cut visibility to under 600 meters within minutes. The enemy may use one to mask his approach to the switchback cut, or it may strand his force on the open lower shelf at your mercy. The weather belongs to neither side.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll 1d6 at the start of each engagement: on 1-3 a blizzard is active, halving all detection and visual ranges and removing the upper shelf's observation advantage for 1d3 turns.

complications.name: The Depleted Company
complications.text: The house company recovering at the upper-shelf fort lost its colors to this same enemy and lost good crews with them. They are 8 'Mechs, Regular quality, with morale wounded in a way no field repair touches. They will fight, but their first instinct under fire is the memory of the last defeat.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The allied house company begins the engagement with a -1 morale modifier; it is removed if your command lands the first confirmed kill, or worsens to -2 if the enemy draws first blood against any allied unit.

decisionPoints.name: Where the Duel Happens
decisionPoints.context: {NPC:opfor-commander} is coming to fight in the open, on the lower shelf, where his honor is satisfied and his numbers tell. You can meet him there, hold the switchback cut and force him to fight on a frontage one lance wide, or refuse the ground entirely and let him come to the fort — each choice reads differently to the watching district.

options.title: Meet Him on the Lower Shelf
advantages: The cleanest possible honor result — open ground, full view, no terrain advantage taken
A decisive win here ends the cycle most completely
disadvantages: His numbers and his fresh crews fight your depleted company on equal terms
No fallback if the wounded company breaks
options.consequence: You fight the duel he wants, on the ground he chose; the honor reward is maximal and so is the risk to your understrength force.

costs.resource: morale exposure: the depleted company fights its tormentor on open ground with no terrain to lean on
costs.risk: If the wounded company breaks in the open, there is no line to fall back to and the rout is total

options.title: Hold the Switchback Cut
advantages: A 14-meter frontage lets one lance fight his whole force in sequence
Honor-conventions intact — it is terrain, not fortification
disadvantages: A patient enemy may decline the cut and raid the herders' lower shelf to bait you down
Holding the cut concedes the initiative and the moral high ground of meeting him openly
options.consequence: You fight on favorable ground but on the defensive; the district notes that you chose advantage over a clean meeting, a smaller restoration of face.

costs.resource: engineering: clearing and revetting the switchback for a defensive stand
costs.risk: He declines the cut, burns the lower shelf grazing, and dares you to come down — every hour you hold is an hour the herders pay for

options.title: Refuse the Ground, Defend the Fort
advantages: Forces him to attack you across open approaches to the upper-shelf fort
Preserves the depleted company behind known ground
disadvantages: Reads as the garrison hiding from the challenge — the warlord's worst outcome short of defeat
Surrenders the steppe and the herders to the enemy's free movement
options.consequence: You may win the fight and lose the campaign; defending the fort against an honor challenge is the dishonor the warlord warned against, even without firing an emplacement.

costs.resource: political capital: refusing open battle spends the district's patience whatever the tactical result
costs.risk: Even a clean defensive victory is logged as having shamed the district a second time

entries.event: Herder runners reach the upper-shelf fort: {NPC:opfor-commander}'s force is on the lower shelf, formed for battle, broadcasting a challenge in clear on the district honor frequency.
Enemy 'Mech force advances to the base of the escarpment; a blizzard front is building off the upper shelf.
Enemy lead lance reaches the switchback-cut approach; if unopposed it begins the climb to the upper shelf and the fort.
If the garrison has not committed to ground by now, the enemy interprets silence as refusal and begins burning the lower-shelf grazing to force a response.
Full enemy force can reach the fort's outer approaches; the honor window closes and the engagement becomes a straightforward defense of the fort.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The garrison must commit to its chosen ground and make contact by T+20:00. Wait longer and {NPC:opfor-commander} reads the delay as refusing the challenge. He burns the grazing, and the secondary honor objective fails before a shot is fired.

opforSketch.composition: One reinforced 'Mech company (9 to 12 machines) at Regular-to-Veteran quality, weighted toward heavy and medium 'Mechs (45-75 tons), led by {NPC:opfor-commander} in a command heavy. No vehicles, no aerospace, no infantry committed — this is a declared honor engagement and the enemy holds to the convention as strictly as the warlord demands of you. Fresh crews, intact morale, a grievance to settle.
opforSketch.behavior: Honor-challenge doctrine: advance openly, accept the duel on declared terms, and fight to a decisive result rather than a raid's quick withdrawal. {NPC:opfor-commander} fights from the front and does not break at the usual thresholds — his force holds to 60 percent damage before any withdrawal, and he personally will not retreat while his command 'Mech is mobile.

forks.name: OPERATION CLOSED LEDGER
forks.trigger: Enemy force decisively defeated within the honor conventions and {NPC:opfor-commander} broken — captured, killed, or routed beyond return.
forks.consequence: The cycle ends here. The district's face is restored and the warlord, satisfied, entrusts your command with cadre authority to rebuild the colorless house company into a unit worth its standard again.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND STEPPE
forks.trigger: Enemy repulsed and the honor conventions kept, but {NPC:opfor-commander} withdraws his force intact and unbroken.
forks.consequence: He has the measure of you now and will return with the lesson learned — a heavier, less ceremonious push that drops the honor pretense. Your command garrisons against a real assault next.

forks.name: OPERATION TWICE SHAMED
forks.trigger: Garrison defeated, or the honor conventions broken even in victory.
forks.consequence: The district is shamed a second time and the warlord must answer to his own superiors. Your command is committed to a desperate counter-raid into {TARGET_FACTION} territory to recover the lost honor by force — a deep strike against odds.

storyElementSeed: A pilot from the colorless company sits in his cockpit on the upper shelf, watching the enemy form up below. He recognizes the paint scheme of the machine that took his unit's standard, and waits for the order. Down the line, the operations officer asks the warlord about the fort guns one more time, and is refused one more time.

is-davion.objectives.secondary: The political read matters more than the kill count. Win it clean — 'Mech against 'Mech, no fort guns, no tanks on the line — or the district decides you saved the fort and lost the point. Pragmatism here is knowing which fight you are actually in.
