HERD_HEAD.unit: head of cattle on the lower shelf

phases.name: POSTURE — THE STEPPE WATCH
phases.lead: The garrison knows he is coming and roughly when. The work before contact is reading the weather off the escarpment, keeping the herders' goodwill, and steadying a company that remembers losing to this same enemy.

dataBlock.Garrison: Your lance plus a depleted house company of 8 'Mechs, Regular, recovering at the upper-shelf fort
dataBlock.Forbidden assets: Fort fixed defenses and all non-'Mech combat units — warlord's standing order
dataBlock.Weather: Ground blizzards 5 days in 7, visibility under 600m, no warning
dataBlock.Early warning: Herder runners and grazing patterns — the enemy cannot cross the lower shelf unseen

phases.protocol: The challenge will come in clear on the district honor frequency; the warlord requires it be acknowledged in clear, by name, before contact. Codeword IRON STANDARD on the garrison net means the engagement is to be fought strictly to convention — no station may request or fire a fixed emplacement once IRON STANDARD is set.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Why a warlord forbids his own guns: the difference between holding a fort and holding face, and what the district remembers a year later about how the fight was won.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT — THE ANSWER
phases.lead: He forms up on the lower shelf and calls you out. The garrison chooses its ground — open meeting, the switchback cut, or the fort approaches — and the depleted company's nerve is tested in the first exchange.

dataBlock.Switchback cut: 14m switchback ramp, the one vehicle-capable link between shelves — one lance can hold it against a company
dataBlock.Honor window: Contact by T+20:00 or the challenge reads as refused
dataBlock.Morale hinge: First confirmed kill removes the company's -1; first blood against an ally deepens it to -2
dataBlock.Weather roll: Blizzard active on a 1-3 — halves ranges, erases the upper-shelf overwatch

sidebarKernel.kernel: A unit that lost its colors carries the wound into the next fight — what a depleted, grieving company needs in the first sixty seconds of contact to fight as itself again.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — THE LEDGER
phases.lead: The result is read by an audience well beyond the steppe. A decisive, convention-clean win closes the feud; a repulse that lets him withdraw whole only schedules the next round.

dataBlock.Decisive break: {NPC:opfor-commander}'s force holds to 60 percent damage before withdrawal; his command 'Mech leaving the field is the break point
dataBlock.Honor audit: The warlord's observers confirm no fixed fire and no vehicles engaged before any reward is paid
dataBlock.Herder settlement: Lower-shelf grazing rights confirmed to the herders who carried the warning

sidebarKernel.kernel: Reading whether the enemy is broken or merely withdrawn — the signatures of a unit that will not come back versus one that is already planning the next visit.

title: OPERATION GLASS PROVOCATION
skeleton: bait force must provoke one proud commander into personally overcommitting his reserve by repeating an insult, holding the pursuit on punishing terrain for a fixed window while fighting too well kills the trap and fighting too poorly reveals it
inspiration: the feigned retreat at Hastings, 1066 (a deliberately convincing rout used to draw a disciplined defender off prepared ground)
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. {NPC:opfor-commander} is the {TARGET_FACTION} battalion commander holding the uplands. His service file marks him proud, impatient, and easily insulted. {EMPLOYER} wants him drawn out of his prepared positions and made to commit his reserve where {EMPLOYER}'s main force can destroy it. Your command is the bait. You will stage a provoking demonstration against the upland garrison. The point is not to take ground; it is to sting the commander's pride until he chases you in person. He will read the raid as contempt and answer it 'Mech against 'Mech, because he will not stoop to replying with artillery. The terrain problem is the glass plain: a 30-kilometer stretch of ground fused into black glass by an orbital strike centuries ago. It rings under a 'Mech's tread and shatters into ankle-deep blades wherever weight bears down. The glass will carry 'Mechs, but it punishes maneuver. Sharp turns and jump landings crack the surface and cost footing, and the sound of movement across it carries for kilometers. {NPC:intel-source} reports that {NPC:opfor-commander} keeps a heavy pursuit lance ready at all times to answer raids. A raid two months ago escaped clean and left him hunting the unit responsible. That grudge is your lever. Your raid must clearly be the same insult, repeated, so he commits not just the duty lance but his pride and his reserve. Then you must hold his attention and draw his pursuit across the glass toward {EMPLOYER}'s killing ground at the narrows, and keep it there for 40 minutes. That is long enough to pull his reserve out of position, but not so long that your bait force is destroyed. Here is the danger: every act that makes the bait more convincing pulls your lance deeper into a fight you are ordered neither to win nor to lose cleanly. No civilians are here. The glass supports nothing, and the same strike that made it emptied the uplands. The only witnesses are the man you are baiting and the force waiting to spring the trap.

objectives.primary: Provoke {NPC:opfor-commander} into committing his pursuit lance and reserve to a personal chase, drawing them across the glass plain toward the narrows for a sustained 40-minute window.
objectives.secondary: Preserve the bait force — extract with no 'Mech lost, so the deception survives to be used again and the unit is not consumed for one engagement.
objectives.bonus: Lure {NPC:opfor-commander}'s own command 'Mech into the narrows kill zone personally, decapitating the upland battalion in {EMPLOYER}'s ambush.

complications.name: The Glass Underfoot
complications.text: Movement across the glass plain rings for kilometers and cracks the surface where weight bears down. Jump jets and hard turns shatter the glass and cost footing. So the glass tells the enemy where you are, and every evasive move risks a fall.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any jump landing or rapid-turn maneuver on Glass hexes requires a piloting check at +2 difficulty; failure costs the 'Mech its movement next turn. The enemy always knows the bait force's hex unless it is stationary.

complications.name: Too Convincing a Bait
complications.text: A bait that works pulls the enemy in hard, and the balance is delicate. Fight too well and you kill the chase, because a destroyed pursuit lance never reaches the narrows. Fight too poorly and the commander guesses it is a trap. One bad exchange either way can lose the whole plan.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the bait force destroys more than one enemy 'Mech before reaching the narrows, the enemy commander breaks off the pursuit, suspecting an ambush, and the primary objective fails. The bait must lose convincingly without dying.

complications.name: The Patient Lance
complications.text: Not every officer takes the bait. {NPC:opfor-commander} may send his duty lance and hold his reserve, reading the raid as a probe. If his pride loses to his professionalism even once, the diversion delivers nothing and {EMPLOYER}'s main effort strikes an intact reserve.
complications.mechanicalEffect: At T+12:00, roll 2d6 with a +2 modifier if the bait force has inflicted at least one casualty or struck a prestige target: on 8 or higher the commander commits his reserve; on 7 or lower he sends only the duty lance and the diversion partially fails.

decisionPoints.name: Setting the Hook
decisionPoints.context: The provocation must be unmistakably personal — the same insult, repeated, aimed at the man rather than the garrison. How you bait him determines whether he commits his pride or merely his duty roster.

options.title: Strike His Prestige Target
advantages: Hitting his personal command post or trophy hangar guarantees the insult lands
Maximizes the chance he commits the reserve in a fury
disadvantages: The prestige target is deep in the garrison's prepared positions
Reaching it exposes the bait force to the fixed defenses you must survive
options.consequence: The hook is set deepest but the bait force fights its way out of the garrison's teeth before the chase even begins.

costs.resource: exposure: the bait force enters the garrison's prepared-fire envelope to reach the trophy target
costs.risk: A bait force chewed up inside the garrison may not survive to be chased — the deception dies in the opening move

options.title: Mock Him on the Open Glass
advantages: A taunting demonstration in clear view, just out of reach, with no garrison fires to brave
Keeps the bait force on ground it can run on
disadvantages: A purely theatrical provocation may read as a probe rather than the insult that repeats
Relies entirely on the commander's temper, with no concrete prestige loss to enrage him
options.consequence: The bait force stays whole and mobile but the hook depends on pride alone; a disciplined commander shrugs it off.

costs.resource: uncertainty: the provocation rests entirely on the enemy commander's temperament
costs.risk: If he is having a patient day, the demonstration delivers nothing and the main effort hits an intact reserve

options.title: Mimic the First Raiders' Blazon
advantages: Painting the bait 'Mechs in the earlier raiders' markings makes the insult unmistakably the same
Turns the commander's existing grudge into the engine of the trap
disadvantages: Requires time and paint stores to alter the unit's appearance before insertion
If the deception is ever unmasked, it confirms to the enemy that the two raids were one coordinated effort
options.consequence: The hook leverages his standing humiliation directly, but the unit carries a false identity that, if blown, links the whole campaign together for enemy intelligence.

costs.resource: deception stores: repaint and false transponder codes on every bait 'Mech
costs.risk: An unmasked blazon proves to {TARGET_FACTION} that both raids were one operation — the diversion becomes a confession

entries.event: Bait force makes contact — the provocation lands; the upland garrison sounds and {NPC:opfor-commander}'s duty lance starts engines.
Bait force begins its fighting withdrawal onto the Glass, drawing the duty lance after it; the reserve commander weighs whether to follow.
The reserve-commitment decision resolves — if the hook is set, {NPC:opfor-commander} releases his pursuit reserve onto the Glass.
Pursuit reaches the midpoint of the Glass; the bait force must keep them coming without being run down, the 40-minute window half elapsed.
Pursuit enters the narrows; {EMPLOYER}'s main effort springs the ambush. The bait force's job is done if the reserve is inside the trap.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The pursuit must be drawn into the narrows by T+40:00. {EMPLOYER}'s main force springs the trap at that mark whether the reserve is fully in or not. Any enemy still short of the narrows escapes the ambush and falls on the bait force's exposed flank.

opforSketch.composition: One heavy pursuit lance (60-80 tons) at Veteran quality on instant readiness, backed by a reserve lance of medium-to-heavy 'Mechs (45-70 tons) at Regular quality and {NPC:opfor-commander}'s command heavy. No vehicles — the vitrified Glass shreds tracks and tires, and the commander disdains answering a 'Mech insult with armor. Aggressive, fast, pride-driven.
opforSketch.behavior: Pursuit doctrine warped by grievance: the duty lance gives chase by the book, but {NPC:opfor-commander}, if provoked, abandons caution and drives the reserve forward to catch the unit that humiliated him. He does not break off for damage while he believes he is winning; he breaks off only if he detects the trap, and he is slow to suspect one when his pride is engaged.

forks.name: OPERATION SHATTERED RESERVE
forks.trigger: Reserve fully drawn into the narrows AND {NPC:opfor-commander}'s command 'Mech caught in the kill zone, the upland battalion decapitated.
forks.consequence: With the commander gone and his reserve destroyed, {EMPLOYER} exploits the collapse immediately — your command leads the follow-on assault to seize the now-leaderless uplands before {TARGET_FACTION} can reconstitute.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND HOOK
forks.trigger: Pursuit reserve drawn into the narrows and mauled by the ambush, bait force extracted, but {NPC:opfor-commander} survives.
forks.consequence: He understands now that the raids were bait, and he will hunt the deception unit with cold method instead of hot pride. Your command must run a follow-on diversion against an enemy who has stopped taking the obvious lure.

forks.name: OPERATION UNSPRUNG
forks.trigger: Hook fails to set, bait force destroyed, or the enemy detects the trap and withdraws his reserve intact.
forks.consequence: {NPC:opfor-commander} now has the deception unmasked and an intact reserve. He turns the tables, hunting {EMPLOYER}'s exposed main effort, and your command is committed to a covering recon to find his counter-move before it lands.

storyElementSeed: A bait-force pilot fumbles a turn on the glass on purpose, shedding footing in a spray of black shards exactly as planned. On his rear scope he watches the pursuing lance speed up to close the gap. He has to trust that the men waiting at the narrows are real and ready, and not just a line on a briefing slide.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Make him chase you. Hit his pride hard enough that he commits the reserve, then run — forty minutes onto the Glass and into our narrows. We are not here to win a fight; we are here to deliver his reserve to the men who will.

clan.situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. {EMPLOYER} requires {NPC:opfor-commander} drawn from his prepared ground and his reserve committed where it can be destroyed. This stratagem offends the honor of an open engagement; it is a deception, and you will execute it because the surat you face has earned no better. The glass plain rings beneath the tread and shatters where weight gathers.

DIVERSION_WINDOW_MIN.unit: minutes the pursuit must be held on the Glass

PURSUIT_MECHS.unit: enemy 'Mechs that can be drawn into pursuit

phases.name: INGRESS — SETTING THE HOOK
phases.lead: The bait force inserts and makes itself unmistakably the insult the commander cannot ignore. Everything in this phase is theater aimed at one man's temper.

dataBlock.Provocation type: Prestige strike, open mockery, or mimicked blazon — set before insertion
dataBlock.Glass behavior: Movement rings for kilometers; jumps and hard turns crack footing at +2 piloting difficulty
dataBlock.Commitment check: T+12:00, 2d6 +2 if a casualty or prestige hit was scored — 8+ commits the reserve

phases.protocol: The bait force runs the earlier raiders' false identity throughout; no genuine call-signs cross any net. Codeword OPEN HAND, passed in the clear and contemptuously, is the scripted taunt meant to be intercepted — it names the commander's earlier humiliation directly and is the single most provoking act in the plan.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Baiting a specific man rather than a unit — what in {NPC:opfor-commander}'s file says he will chase, and the difference between an insult he must answer and one he can afford to ignore.

phases.name: GROUND — THE CHASE ON THE GLASS
phases.lead: The bait force runs a fighting withdrawal across thirty kilometers of singing glass, losing convincingly without being caught, keeping the pursuit hot and coming for the full window.

dataBlock.Window: 40 minutes of sustained pursuit from commitment to the narrows
dataBlock.Credibility band: Destroy more than one pursuer and the commander smells the trap and breaks off
dataBlock.Footing penalty: Every evasive maneuver risks a piloting failure that strands the 'Mech for a turn
dataBlock.Pace: Stay caught-but-not-killed — too fast loses him, too slow loses you

sidebarKernel.kernel: The arithmetic of a credible bait: how to lose ground at a rate that keeps a pursuer committed, and why the hardest order to give is hold fire when the shot is there.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — CLEAR OF THE NARROWS
phases.lead: At the narrows {EMPLOYER}'s main effort springs and the bait force's task inverts from running to surviving the moment the trap closes and the enemy realizes what happened.

dataBlock.Spring point: T+40:00 at the narrows — main effort fires whether the reserve is fully in or not
dataBlock.Bait extraction: Bait force peels off the chase line the instant the ambush opens and runs for its own exit
dataBlock.Stragglers: Any pursuer short of the narrows escapes the ambush and falls on the bait force's flank

sidebarKernel.kernel: Getting a hard-run bait force off the Glass intact — the heat, the shed footing, and the cracked actuators a forty-minute fighting withdrawal leaves you to nurse home.

title: OPERATION BAD ATTRIBUTION
skeleton: hunter contracted as reprisal must follow a trail that loops back to its own paymaster, choosing between a clean bounty that buries the truth and an answer that destroys the contract, while the only intelligence source profits from either ending
inspiration: the false-flag provocation pattern of the Gleiwitz incident, 1939 (an attack staged by the very party that later claims to avenge it)
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} occupation border, {YEAR}. Three weeks ago a raiding band hit your unit's camp on {WORLD}, killed two techs, and burned a DropShip cargo bay. {EMPLOYER} has now put your command under contract to find them and finish it, calling the hunt payback for a pirate insult. The contract reads clean. The trail does not. {NPC:intel-source}, a salvage-and-information broker working the system's mining belt, sells you the raiders' likely bolt-hole: a worked-out chromium mine in the badlands, the deep adit. But followed honestly, the same trail keeps bending back toward {EMPLOYER}'s own supply arm. The burned cargo, it turns out, was insured at three times its listed value, and the raiders knew exactly which bay to hit. That tip is 14 days old and shaky, and the source profits no matter how the hunt ends, so weigh it carefully. The terrain problem is the badlands: a maze of chromium-tailings canyons. The ore dust glows under 'Mech spotlights and clogs air filters, cutting engagement range below 500 meters and forcing units single file through slot canyons 8 to 12 meters wide. The deep adit sits at the head of one such slot, a fortified mine mouth a single lance could hold against three times its number. {NPC:intel-source} reports the band as about one lance of mixed 'Mechs plus a hover-armor section running on salvaged parts, Green-to-Regular, fighting like people who want to survive, not win. Here is what the contract leaves out. If the raid was an insurance fraud set up through {EMPLOYER}'s own supply arm, the band you are hunting may be hired subcontractors, and the man paying you to kill them may be the man who hired them. That makes the truth worth more than the bounty, and more dangerous than the fight. A few independent prospectors work the badlands. They owe no one loyalty and will sell either side directions for a little water. The hunt itself is simple. Working out who you are really working for is not.

objectives.primary: Locate, corner, and neutralize the raiding band responsible for the leaguer strike — destroyed, captured, or driven off-world for good.
objectives.secondary: Recover physical evidence of who directed the raid — a contract, a payment record, a prisoner who will talk — before it is destroyed or buried in the deep adit.
objectives.bonus: Confirm or disprove {EMPLOYER}'s involvement in the original strike, and get the proof off-world intact, whatever it costs the contract.

complications.name: The Source's Motive
complications.text: {NPC:intel-source} sells to both sides and profits whichever way the hunt ends. The trail to the deep adit may be true, or a trap to thin your force in the slot canyons, or true but pointed exactly where the broker wants you. And every time you buy directions, you show the broker what you plan to do.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each piece of intelligence bought from {NPC:intel-source} has a hidden reliability: the gamemaster rolls 1d6 per purchase, and on a 1-2 the information is a deliberate steer that places the band's strength or position one band off the truth.

complications.name: Chromium Fog
complications.text: Tailings dust fluoresces under spotlights and fouls intakes. Engagement ranges fall under 500 meters and any sustained movement at speed forces filter purges that vent heat and announce position. The badlands fight is close, blind, and hot.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All detection and weapon ranges in the badlands are reduced to 500 meters maximum; any 'Mech moving at flank speed for two consecutive turns must vent or suffer +3 heat the following turn.

complications.name: The Employer's Shadow
complications.text: If the strike was an insurance arrangement, {EMPLOYER} has every reason to ensure the band dies quietly and the evidence with them. Orders may arrive mid-hunt to destroy rather than capture, to skip the Adit's records, to call it done early. Following them ends the question; refusing them ends the contract.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the secondary or bonus objective is pursued, a mid-mission employer order arrives instructing immediate destruction of the band without capture; complying voids the secondary and bonus, refusing imposes a contract-breach penalty and shifts the resolution to the FAILURE-adjacent fork.

decisionPoints.name: Working the Trail
decisionPoints.context: The deep adit is where the trail points, but the trail bends back toward your own employer at every honest reading. You can take the band the fast way and not ask, dig for the truth at the cost of speed, or hedge — and the badlands punish indecision with ambush.

options.title: Hit the Adit Fast, Ask Nothing
advantages: Fastest route to the bounty and the contract's clean closure
Denies the band time to scatter into the canyon maze
disadvantages: A frontal assault on a fortified mine mouth in a slot canyon is the band's best chance to bleed you
Whatever the strike really was dies with the band and the records
options.consequence: You collect the bounty and close the contract, but the question of who you worked for stays buried under the deep adit forever.

costs.resource: casualties: a frontal slot-canyon assault on prepared positions is the costliest way in
costs.risk: The Adit's single lane lets a defending lance fight you in detail — the bounty is real but so is the butcher's bill

options.title: Take a Prisoner, Pull the Thread
advantages: A captured raider may name who hired the strike
Evidence off-world is leverage worth more than the bounty
disadvantages: Capture operations are slower and riskier than killing
Pulling the thread puts you crosswise with the man signing your checks
options.consequence: You may learn the truth and you may regret learning it; the contract sours the moment {EMPLOYER} senses you are asking questions.

costs.resource: operational risk: capture-and-interrogate doubles the time on a hostile, blind battlefield
costs.risk: An employer who arranged the strike will not pay the unit that proves it — the bounty may evaporate with the truth

options.title: Buy the Full Picture First
advantages: A complete intelligence package from {NPC:intel-source} may reveal the band's true strength and backer before you commit
Reduces the chance of walking into a steered ambush
disadvantages: {NPC:intel-source} charges premium for the full file and may be selling it to the band too
Every day spent buying intelligence is a day the band uses to dig in or flee
options.consequence: You go in better informed but poorer, and you have handed your only intelligence source proof of exactly what you intend to do.

costs.resource: trust: the source now knows your full intent and can sell it onward
costs.risk: The full picture may itself be the steer — a premium price is no guarantee of premium truth from a broker who serves both sides

entries.event: Lead element enters the badlands; chromium fog active, the band's lookouts among the prospector camps mark your arrival within the hour.
The band knows it is hunted; raiders begin staging at the deep adit and rigging the mine's record cache for destruction.
If no employer interference has arrived, the slot-canyon approach to the Adit is in contact; the defending lance fights from the mine mouth.
Record cache destruction completes if the Adit is not taken by now — the evidence of who directed the strike is lost.
The band's hover section attempts to break out the rear adit and scatter into the canyon maze; the chance to corner them whole closes.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The deep adit must be entered and its record cache secured by T+24:00. Later than that, the raiders finish destroying it, and the evidence is gone for good, along with any answer about who really ordered the strike on your camp.

opforSketch.composition: One mixed 'Mech lance (30-55 tons, salvage-built and mismatched) at Green-to-Regular quality, supported by a hover-armor section of 3 to 4 vehicles (Pegasus/Saracen behavior) running on cannibalized parts. Defending a fortified mine mouth on a single-lane approach. Underequipped, under-crewed, fighting from prepared ground because they cannot win in the open.
opforSketch.behavior: Survival doctrine, not victory doctrine: the band fights to make the hunt too expensive to finish, holds the Adit's choke as long as it pays, and runs the instant the cost-benefit turns against them. They break contact at 30 percent force damage and have a rehearsed breakout through the rear adit. They will surrender if cornered and offered terms — they fight to live, not to die.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN BOUNTY
forks.trigger: Band neutralized and the contract closed; the question of who ordered the strike left unasked or unanswered.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER}, satisfied and relieved, extends the contract — a follow-on pirate-suppression sweep of the system's mining belt that keeps your command paid and conveniently far from the questions you did not ask.

forks.name: OPERATION PAPER TRAIL
forks.trigger: Band neutralized, the Adit's records secured, AND proof of {EMPLOYER}'s involvement recovered intact and off-world.
forks.consequence: You hold leverage over the man who hired you. The proof becomes the lever for a high-stakes extraction — pulling a witness or a second record set off-world before {EMPLOYER} can bury the evidence and the people who carried it.

forks.name: OPERATION BURNED CONTRACT
forks.trigger: Band escapes, the unit is mauled in the slot canyons, or {EMPLOYER} terminates the contract when the unit asks too many questions.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} cuts the contract and quietly marks your command a liability. The band — or {EMPLOYER}'s next subcontractors — come for you on the back foot, and your command fights a defensive action with its reputation and its pay both at risk.

storyElementSeed: A captured raider, cornered in the mine mouth with chromium dust glowing on his armor, looks at the merc commander. He says he was paid in Lyran kroner that came through the same bank as the contract. Then he waits to learn whether that fact buys him a seat off the planet or a grave in the tailings.

is-steiner.objectives.bonus: If the insurance fraud reaches into a noble house's logistics concern, the proof is worth more than the mine and the band combined — handled correctly, it is a debt the house will pay for years to keep quiet. Recover it; the social ledger here outvalues the bounty.

BADLANDS_RANGE_M.unit: meters maximum engagement range in chromium fog

SLOT_CANYON_WIDTH_M.unit: meters width of the Adit approach canyon

INSURANCE_MULTIPLE.unit: times manifest value the burned cargo was insured for

resourceGates.lackingText: Treasury short of 35,000 C-bills: {NPC:intel-source} will sell only a partial file for 12,000. It confirms the band's position but leaves out their strength and their backer, so you go in still guessing about the two things that matter most.

phases.name: INGRESS — INTO THE BADLANDS
phases.lead: The hunt begins blind, in fluorescing dust, against a band that knows the canyons and a source who knows your wallet. The trail points one way and bends another.

dataBlock.Visibility: Under 500m in chromium fog; spotlights betray position
dataBlock.Source reliability: Each purchase a 1-in-3 chance of a deliberate steer
dataBlock.Filter penalty: Two turns at flank forces a heat-venting purge
dataBlock.Prospector camps: Independent, for sale to either side, the band's early warning net

routes.name: AMBER — THE SLOT TO THE ADIT
routes.desc: The direct single-lane canyon to the fortified mine mouth
routes.tradeoff: Fastest to the band; the one ground where a single defending lance can fight you in detail

routes.name: OCHRE — THE TAILINGS TRAVERSE
routes.desc: A longer route over open tailings fields to the Adit's flank
routes.tradeoff: Avoids the choke but crosses ground where the hover section can run and harry you in the fog

phases.protocol: Reprisal cover-story discipline: the contract is public as pirate-suppression, and the unit keeps it that way on all open nets even after the trail bends toward {EMPLOYER}. Codeword DRY WELL, on the command channel, means the trail has been confirmed as a probable employer steer — at DRY WELL the unit shifts to securing evidence over collecting the bounty.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Reading a double-dealing broker: the tells that separate a true steer from a paid one, and why the most reliable information is often the piece the source did not want to sell.

phases.name: GROUND — THE ADIT
phases.lead: The band fights from the mine mouth to make the hunt too costly to finish. The choice between killing them fast and taking them whole is also the choice between closing the contract and opening the question.

dataBlock.Defensive choke: Single-lane mine mouth, a lance can hold against three times its number
dataBlock.Record cache: Destroyed by T+24:00 if the Adit is not taken — the evidence clock
dataBlock.Breakout: Rear adit, hover section scatters into the maze at 30 percent force damage
dataBlock.Surrender: The band takes terms if cornered — they fight to live

sidebarKernel.kernel: When the cheap victory is the wrong one: weighing a clean bounty against the cost of never knowing who you actually fought for, and the orders you may get to keep it that way.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — WHAT LEAVES PANDORA
phases.lead: Whatever you carry off {WORLD} — a bounty, a prisoner, a record cache, or a dangerous truth — decides which contract you are really finishing and who your next enemy is.

dataBlock.Evidence handling: Records and prisoners moved off-world before {EMPLOYER} can intercept
dataBlock.Employer order risk: A destroy-don't-capture order may arrive mid-extraction

sidebarKernel.kernel: Getting a witness and a record cache off a world where your employer controls the spaceport — the quiet logistics of leaving with something the man who hired you wants buried.

title: OPERATION PARADE GROUND
skeleton: rescuers must pull non-ambulatory captives from a detention site staged as bait before a humiliation broadcast, where the whole operation is filmed and a failure on camera is a worse defeat than no attempt at all
inspiration: the Son Tay raid, 1970 (a daring prison rescue against a site the enemy had effectively prepared, where the political stakes outweighed the bodies recovered)
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} occupation border, {YEAR}. Two weeks ago a botched probe cost your command four MechWarriors, captured by {TARGET_FACTION}. {NPC:opfor-commander}, the occupying garrison commander, has announced a victory parade in the provincial capital in six days. He plans to march the prisoners through the city square in chains, on camera, to wreck your unit's standing with {EMPLOYER} and the nobility who pay it. {EMPLOYER}, a march-lord whose reputation is tied to yours, wants the prisoners out before the parade. A rescue turns his shame into a triumph, while a parade that goes ahead is a wound that never fully heals. The terrain problem is the city ringbahn: an elevated electric rail loop that circles the old city core on a 12-meter stone viaduct. It is the only route to the central detention barracks that a 'Mech can take without flattening the historic streets the nobility prize. The viaduct carries the rail and blocks movement beneath it, so any approach to the barracks funnels through two arched underpasses, each wide enough for one 'Mech at a time. {NPC:intel-source}, a rail-yard dispatcher feeding the local resistance, reports the prisoners in the barracks' east cell block and the parade staging in the cathedral square 600 meters away. He puts the garrison reaction force at one 'Mech lance plus a wheeled-armor company, quartered at the rail yard. That report is 4 days old. The prisoners are in poor shape: two weeks of interrogation, one with a leg wound that cannot take a march, and none able to pilot a 'Mech out even if one waited. They leave in a vehicle or they do not leave. There is a trap here. {NPC:opfor-commander} expects a rescue and wants one. The parade is partly bait, and the prisoners are deliberately held somewhere a raider can reach, because catching the rescue force on camera is a bigger win for him than the parade alone. The city holds 200,000 residents under occupation. Sullen and watching, they will neither help nor hinder until they see who is winning. Six days to the parade, or fewer if {NPC:opfor-commander} moves it up.

objectives.primary: Extract all four captured MechWarriors from the city detention barracks and off-world before the victory parade, alive and free.
objectives.secondary: Withdraw the raiding force without a unit captured or destroyed on camera — a filmed rescue failure is worse for {EMPLOYER} than no attempt at all.
objectives.bonus: Disrupt or pre-empt the parade itself so visibly that {NPC:opfor-commander}'s intended humiliation rebounds on him in the same news cycle.

complications.name: The Rescue Is Expected
complications.text: {NPC:opfor-commander} has set the prisoners where a raider can reach them on purpose. The parade is bait; the real prize is a rescue force caught on camera. Every approach that looks obvious is obvious because he wants you to take it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the raiding force uses the most direct approach to the barracks, the gamemaster deploys a concealed reaction element on its flank that activates on contact; a less obvious approach trades time for avoiding the prepared trap.

complications.name: Prisoners Cannot Walk Out
complications.text: Two weeks of interrogation have left all four prisoners unfit to march and one with a leg wound. They require vehicle transport from the cell block to the extraction point; a 'Mech cannot carry four broken people through a firefight, and there is no time to wait for them to recover.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The raiding force must include or seize a transport vehicle to move the prisoners; if the transport is destroyed before extraction, the prisoners cannot be moved and the primary objective fails.

complications.name: The Watching City
complications.text: Two hundred thousand city residents are watching, and so are {NPC:opfor-commander}'s cameras. A clean rescue swings the city and the news cycle to {EMPLOYER}; a bungled one filmed in the cathedral square is the propaganda victory the parade was meant to be, delivered for free.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any raiding unit destroyed or captured within camera range of the cathedral square voids the secondary objective and shifts the resolution toward the COMPROMISED fork regardless of whether the prisoners are recovered.

decisionPoints.name: The Way In
decisionPoints.context: The detention barracks can only be reached through the Ringbahn's two undercrossings, each one 'Mech wide, both of which {NPC:opfor-commander} has surely covered. You can force the obvious one, find a way the viaduct was not built to allow, or skip the barracks approach entirely and take the prisoners in transit.

options.title: Force the East Undercrossing
advantages: Shortest line to the east cell block where the prisoners are held
A single-file choke cuts both ways — it limits the reaction force's ability to swarm you
disadvantages: This is the approach {NPC:opfor-commander} expects and has trapped
A 'Mech stuck in the undercrossing under fire is the parade footage he wants
options.consequence: You take the fast road into a prepared kill zone; speed buys the cell block but at the price of fighting on his chosen ground.

costs.resource: exposure: the lead 'Mech enters the undercrossing in single file, into pre-sited fires
costs.risk: A 'Mech down in the arch is the centerpiece of the very propaganda the rescue exists to prevent

options.title: Drop the Viaduct, Make a New Door
advantages: A demolished viaduct span opens an approach the garrison has not covered
Severs the elevated rail the reaction force uses to shift troops
disadvantages: Bringing down a 12-meter masonry span in a treasured medieval city enrages the Lyran nobility {EMPLOYER} answers to
The demolition is loud and starts the reaction clock before the barracks is even reached
options.consequence: You buy a fresh approach at the cost of the architecture the margrave's peers prize; the rescue may succeed and the social bill may swallow the credit.

costs.resource: demolition stores and a noble-relations debt for wrecking historic infrastructure
costs.risk: The nobility {EMPLOYER} serves may resent a leveled landmark more than they value four rescued pilots

options.title: Take Them at the Parade Marshalling
advantages: The prisoners are out of the fortified barracks when staged for the parade — softer to seize
A snatch in the staging yard pre-empts the humiliation at its source
disadvantages: The marshalling yard is yards from the garrison's full assembled strength
The timing window is minutes wide and tied to {NPC:opfor-commander}'s schedule, which he can change
options.consequence: You hit them where they are weakest and most watched at once; success is a public triumph, failure is the most public failure possible.

costs.resource: timing risk: the snatch window is minutes wide and set by the enemy's clock
costs.risk: If {NPC:opfor-commander} moves the parade up or changes the route, the whole plan is built on a schedule that no longer exists

entries.event: Raiding force commits to the city core; rail-yard garrison detects the approach and the reaction lance starts engines.
Wheeled-armor company moves to seal the Ringbahn undercrossings; concealed flank element activates if the obvious approach was taken.
Raiding force must be at the east cell block and the prisoners loading by now to clear the city before the garrison concentrates.
Garrison reaction force can fight as a combined arm at the barracks; the cathedral-square cameras are live and rolling.
Full garrison response seals the city core's exits; any raiding force still inside the Ringbahn is trapped on camera.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The prisoners must be loaded and the transport moving toward the extraction point by T+11:00. Miss it and the garrison seals the ringbahn underpasses at T+26:00, trapping the rescue force inside the city core and handing {NPC:opfor-commander} an even bigger triumph than the parade.

opforSketch.composition: One garrison 'Mech lance (40-65 tons) at Regular quality, supported by a wheeled-armor company of 6 to 9 vehicles (Condor/Manticore behavior) quartered at the rail yard, plus a concealed reaction element held specifically to spring on a rescue force. Defending an urban detention site with prepared positions at the Ringbahn undercrossings. Disciplined, camera-conscious, expecting the attempt.
opforSketch.behavior: Counter-rescue doctrine: the garrison wants the raiders caught on film, not merely repulsed, so it funnels the approach into covered ground and springs the concealed element only when the rescue force is committed and visible. The wheeled armor screens and seals exits rather than charging. The garrison fights to entrap rather than to destroy, and presses hardest when the cathedral cameras have line of sight; it breaks off only if the prisoners are clearly gone and the propaganda lost.

forks.name: OPERATION REVERSED REEL
forks.trigger: All four prisoners extracted alive AND the parade pre-empted so visibly that {NPC:opfor-commander}'s humiliation rebounds on him.
forks.consequence: The propaganda coup is total. {EMPLOYER}, his standing soaring, backs an immediate exploitation — your command leads a follow-on raid to seize a garrison depot the embarrassed {NPC:opfor-commander} has been ordered to defend at all costs.

forks.name: OPERATION QUIET RETURN
forks.trigger: Prisoners extracted and the raiding force withdrawn off-camera, but the parade proceeds for the city's other cameras.
forks.consequence: The rescue worked but {NPC:opfor-commander} saves face with the parade's empty pageantry. Stung, he tightens the occupation and your command is pulled into a security posting to shield the local resistance cell that made the rescue possible from his reprisal sweep.

forks.name: OPERATION FILMED DEFEAT
forks.trigger: Rescue fails, a unit is caught on camera, or the prisoners are not recovered.
forks.consequence: {NPC:opfor-commander} has his footage and {EMPLOYER} his ruin. With its reputation gutted, your command must run a deep diversionary raid to draw the triumphant garrison off-balance long enough to recover the prisoners by a second, desperate try.

storyElementSeed: A rescued pilot is half-carried into the seized transport. Through the cargo slats he sees the cathedral square's parade banners already strung between the lampposts. He asks the trooper buckling him in whether anyone got the cameras, because who owns the footage will decide whether this was a rescue or a recruiting film for the other side.

is-marik.objectives.primary: The Captain-General's provinces are watching how the League treats its own. Get all four out and home before the parade — a rescue is the rebuttal, and the rebuttal is owed to the families and the provincial assemblies as much as to {EMPLOYER}.

GARRISON_VEHICLES.unit: garrison armor vehicles at the rail yard

assetDetails.detail: Leg wound from interrogation will not bear weight; requires litter transport and cannot self-extract from the cell block to the transport vehicle.
Rail-yard dispatcher feeding the resistance — provides the cell-block location and parade schedule but cannot vouch for whether {NPC:opfor-commander} has moved the parade up since the last report.

phases.name: INGRESS — THE RINGBAHN
phases.lead: The elevated rail loop is wall, road, and trap at once. The raiding force commits to one of the two single-file undercrossings, or to making a third way the garrison has not covered, before it ever reaches the prisoners.

dataBlock.Viaduct: 12m masonry, two undercrossings each one 'Mech wide, the only 'Mech routes into the core
dataBlock.Cell block: Barracks east block, 600m from the cathedral-square parade staging
dataBlock.Reaction force: 1 'Mech lance plus a 6-9 vehicle wheeled company at the rail yard, plus a concealed counter-rescue element
dataBlock.Transport requirement: Prisoners move by vehicle or not at all

routes.name: GRAY — EAST UNDERCROSSING
routes.desc: The direct single-file arch to the east cell block
routes.tradeoff: Shortest to the prisoners; the approach {NPC:opfor-commander} has trapped

routes.name: SLATE — WEST UNDERCROSSING + STREET LOOP
routes.desc: The far arch and a longer loop through the old streets
routes.tradeoff: Avoids the prepared trap but adds time and risks building damage in the prized medieval core

phases.protocol: Off-camera discipline governs everything: the unit assumes every minute in the core is filmed and plays to that. Codeword DARK LANTERN on the raid net means the cathedral-square cameras have line of sight on a friendly unit — at DARK LANTERN no unit may be left immobilized in the open and the priority shifts to clearing the camera arc even ahead of pace.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Why the prisoners are held somewhere reachable on purpose — reading a bait-rescue, and the difference between an approach that is open and one that is left open.

phases.name: GROUND — THE CELL BLOCK
phases.lead: Four broken pilots, one transport, a counter-rescue element waiting to spring, and a clock tied to a parade the enemy can move. The snatch is the easy part; getting four people who cannot walk into a vehicle under fire is not.

dataBlock.Prisoner state: All four unfit to march, one litter-bound — vehicle extraction mandatory
dataBlock.Trap trigger: Concealed element springs on the obvious approach when the rescue force is committed and visible
dataBlock.Loading deadline: Prisoners loaded and transport moving by T+11:00
dataBlock.Camera arc: Cathedral square cameras live from T+18:00 — anything lost in frame is lost twice

sidebarKernel.kernel: Moving four interrogation casualties under fire — the litter case, the loading order, and why the rescue's tempo is set by the slowest body, not the fastest 'Mech.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — OFF THE REEL
phases.lead: The transport runs for the edge of the ringbahn while the garrison tries to seal the core and the cameras try to catch a loss. What leaves the city, and whose footage it leaves in, decides the whole campaign's next turn.

dataBlock.Seal deadline: Garrison closes the undercrossings at T+26:00 — be clear of the loop before it shuts
dataBlock.Camera resolution: A clean off-camera withdrawal swings the news cycle; a filmed loss hands it back
dataBlock.Parade pre-emption: A visible disruption of the staging square converts the rescue into a public triumph

sidebarKernel.kernel: Winning the news cycle as a military objective — why a rescue that nobody films and a rescue that everybody films are two different victories, and which one {EMPLOYER} actually bought.

title: OPERATION BLOODED REMATCH
skeleton: commander must blood green warriors in the same ritual rematch that decides a contested bloodline's claim, where teaching and fighting are one act and the bid he answers sets whether the untested have any chance at all
inspiration: the Roman gladiatorial ludus and the duel of honor's escalation (a contest where a defeated line's right to its name is wagered on a rematch the loser's house demands)
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} occupation zone, {YEAR}. One season ago a Trial of Grievance ended with your sibko-mate defeated and a bloodname-bearing 'Mech forfeited to a rival Cluster. The bloodhouse will not let it rest. {NPC:opfor-commander}, a Star Commander of the rival line, has issued a fresh batchall, the formal Clan challenge. He has called a Trial of Refusal, dressed as a training exercise turned into a grievance. Your warriors must answer for the earlier loss on harder terms, with the bid raised and the bloodname's honor at stake again. {EMPLOYER}, your own Star Colonel, has placed you over a Star of newly-blooded warriors, fresh from their Trials of Position. You must drill them and test them against this rematch. Here the teaching and the fighting are one act: the Clans train a warrior by making him face what would kill an untrained one. The terrain problem is the caldera testing range, a Clan exercise ground built in the broken crater of a dead volcano. The only level fighting platforms are basalt benches, split by lava-tube ravines too deep to cross and too narrow to see into. A Star deploys across three benches. A single rock bridge links each pair, and a warrior pushed off a bench has nowhere to fall but the ravine. {NPC:intel-source}, your own Cluster's tech caste, who service both sides' machines, reports that {NPC:opfor-commander} will bid down to a Star of heavy 'Mechs, Veteran quality, hand-picked for the grudge. He means to win cleanly enough to claim the contested bloodname outright. That report is 5 days old and rated reliable. What no batchall says aloud: losing a Trial a second time does not just forfeit a 'Mech. It discredits the bloodline's right to the name. Your green Star carries that weight into a fight it is barely ready for. No civilians are here. The caldera holds only the testing range and the watching warriors of both Clusters, whose witness makes the result binding. The bid is set and the honor is real. The warriors you must blood may not survive the lesson.

objectives.primary: Win the Trial of Refusal against {NPC:opfor-commander}'s Star, defending the contested bloodname and the honor of your line.
objectives.secondary: Bring the newly-blooded Star through the Trial as a functioning combat unit — losses are expected, but the Star must emerge tested and cohesive, not shattered.
objectives.bonus: Defeat {NPC:opfor-commander} personally, in single combat within the larger Trial, settling the grievance so decisively that the rival line cannot re-open it.

complications.name: The Bid and the Bloodname
complications.text: {NPC:opfor-commander} has bid down to a Star of hand-picked Veteran heavies and means to claim the contested bloodname by winning. A second defeat does not forfeit one machine; it discredits the bloodline's claim to the name itself. The stakes are not equipment but lineage.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the Trial is lost, the bonus and secondary are forfeit and the campaign's reputation track takes a permanent loss; the rival line gains standing that shapes future Clan-register missions toward the FAILURE fork.

complications.name: The Caldera Benches
complications.text: The testing range is three basalt benches over lava-tube ravines, each connected by a single rock bridge. A warrior pushed off a bench falls into a ravine too deep to climb out of and too narrow to fight in. Position on the benches is everything; a bridge held is a flank secured.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each rock bridge is a single-'Mech chokepoint; a 'Mech forced off a bench edge by knockdown or push is removed from the engagement. Control of the bridges determines which benches each Star can reinforce.

complications.name: Green Warriors, Veteran Foe
complications.text: Your Star is fresh from Trials of Position: skilled, eager, and never tested in a fight meant to kill them. {NPC:opfor-commander}'s warriors were hand-picked for this grudge and want it badly. Trained is not the same as blooded, and this Trial closes that gap the hard way, under real fire.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The friendly Star begins at a piloting/gunnery disadvantage versus the Veteran enemy; each turn a green warrior survives in direct combat improves their effective skill by a step, capping at Regular, modeling the blooding under fire.

decisionPoints.name: Answering the Bid
decisionPoints.context: {NPC:opfor-commander} has bid down to a Star of heavies and named the caldera range. Clan honor permits you to accept the bid, counter-bid to reshape the Trial, or invoke a point of grievance that changes its terms — each choice is read by the watching warriors as a statement about your line's confidence.

options.title: Accept the Bid as Stated
advantages: The cleanest honor — meeting the challenge on its stated terms wins maximum standing
No counter-bid means no concession of weakness before the watching Clusters
disadvantages: Your green Star fights Veteran heavies with no terms adjusted in its favor
{NPC:opfor-commander} chose these terms because they favor him
options.consequence: You fight the Trial he designed, and a win on his own terms is the most decisive answer possible — if your warriors survive to deliver it.

costs.resource: honor stake: accepting unadjusted terms wagers the bloodname on a green Star against a chosen one
costs.risk: He set these terms to win them — accepting is fighting on the ground of his choosing with the lineage on the scales

options.title: Counter-Bid the Engagement Down
advantages: Bidding to fewer or lighter machines can equalize a green Star against Veterans
Demonstrates confidence — winning with less is the highest Clan honor
disadvantages: A failed counter-bid that loses still loses the bloodname, now with less force to win it
Bidding too low to look bold can hand {NPC:opfor-commander} the Trial outright
options.consequence: You reshape the Trial toward your warriors' strengths at the cost of fielding less to win it; the watching warriors weigh the boldness against the risk.

costs.resource: force committed: a counter-bid that wins honor wins it by fielding fewer machines than the foe
costs.risk: Bid too low for honor's sake and a green Star wins nothing because there was never enough of it on the benches

options.title: Invoke a Point of Grievance on the Terms
advantages: A legitimate procedural challenge can force the Trial onto neutral ground or a fairer bid
Buys the green Star time to drill before the rematch
disadvantages: Invoking procedure against a batchall reads as reluctance to fight — a stain the watching Clusters remember
{NPC:opfor-commander} may answer the procedural challenge with a personal one, raising the stakes again
options.consequence: You improve the Trial's fairness at the cost of your line's reputation for eagerness; among warriors who prize the charge, hesitation is its own defeat.

costs.resource: reputation: a procedural challenge spends the line's name for boldness to buy fairer terms
costs.risk: The watching Clusters file the delay as reluctance, and {NPC:opfor-commander} may escalate to a personal grievance that no procedure can soften

entries.event: Both Stars deploy across the caldera benches; {NPC:opfor-commander} states the bid in the formal batchall and the watching Clusters fall silent.
First contact across the central bridges; the green Star's blooding begins as the Veterans press for a bench.
Control of at least one central rock bridge must be established by now, or the enemy Star concentrates on a single bench and rolls up the green warriors in detail.
The grievance reaches its crisis — {NPC:opfor-commander} commits to the bench where the contested bloodname's honor is decided; single combat with him is possible from this point.
The Trial resolves by the formal conventions; a Star that has not secured a decisive bench by now has lost the grievance whatever its surviving strength.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: You must win control of a central bridge by T+12:00. Miss it and {NPC:opfor-commander}'s Veteran Star grinds down the green warriors one bench at a time, and the Trial and the bloodname are both lost by attrition before T+28:00.

opforSketch.composition: One Clan Star of five heavy 'Mechs (60-85 tons) at Veteran quality, hand-picked from the rival bloodhouse for the grievance, led by {NPC:opfor-commander} in a command assault or heavy. No vehicles — this is a Trial of Refusal fought strictly 'Mech against 'Mech under Clan honor convention, and no Clan warrior would dishonor a bloodname Trial with armor support. Disciplined, aggressive, contemptuous of the green Star.
opforSketch.behavior: Trial doctrine: engage in formal Clan style, one warrior seeking one opponent, pressing the bridges to concentrate against the weakest bench. {NPC:opfor-commander} fights to claim the bloodname cleanly and will accept a challenge to single combat as the highest honor — but his Star fights to win the grievance, breaking off only at zellbrigen's conventions or a clear decision, not at a damage threshold.

forks.name: OPERATION SETTLED LINE
forks.trigger: Trial won AND {NPC:opfor-commander} defeated in single combat, the grievance settled beyond re-opening.
forks.consequence: The bloodname is secured and the green Star blooded into a unit of standing. {EMPLOYER} entrusts your now-proven Star with a true combat command — a follow-on objective raid into Inner Sphere territory to claim isorla worthy of the line's restored honor.

forks.name: OPERATION THIRD GRIEVANCE
forks.trigger: Trial won and the bloodname defended, but {NPC:opfor-commander} survives unbroken.
forks.consequence: The bloodname holds but the rival line is not satisfied. {NPC:opfor-commander} will find a third pretext, and your command must garrison the line's holdings against the next manufactured grievance while the green Star hardens into veterans.

forks.name: OPERATION FORFEIT NAME
forks.trigger: Trial lost, or the green Star shattered beyond the line's ability to field it.
forks.consequence: The bloodname is discredited and the rival line ascendant. Disgraced, your command is reduced to a solahma posting — a desperate defense against an Inner Sphere counter-push the rival Cluster has left you to absorb alone, the last chance to die with honor restored.

storyElementSeed: A newly-blooded warrior holds a rock bridge alone, watching a Veteran heavy cross the basalt toward her. She remembers her Star Commander's one instruction before the Trial: she was not brought here to win, but to learn whether she can. The lava tube behind her does not care which.

is-kurita.situation: Observed from the Combine's intelligence desk: a Clan bloodhouse in the occupation zone reopens a Trial of Grievance one season after a contested loss, the rival Star Commander {NPC:opfor-commander} staging a Trial of Refusal to claim a bloodname outright. The caldera range gives three basalt fighting benches over lava-tube ravines, a single rock bridge between each. The Clan honor that binds the result is also the seam an outside observer learns to read.

BENCHES.unit: basalt fighting benches in the caldera

BLOODING_TURNS_TO_CAP.unit: turns of survival to harden a green warrior toward Regular

phases.name: POSTURE — THE BATCHALL
phases.lead: The rematch opens with words, not weapons. The bid is answered, the green Star drilled against the terms it will face, and the watching Clusters take the measure of the line before a shot is fired.

dataBlock.The bid: {NPC:opfor-commander} bids down to five Veteran heavies, the caldera range named
dataBlock.Your force: A Star of five newly-blooded warriors, fresh from Trials of Position
dataBlock.The stake: Not a 'Mech but the bloodline's claim to the contested name
dataBlock.Witnesses: Both Clusters watch; their witness makes the result binding

protocol.Batchall: The challenge and bid are stated formally; the answer (accept, counter-bid, or grievance) is given in kind before the Clusters
protocol.Zellbrigen: The Trial is fought one warrior to one opponent; breaking the dueling convention dishonors the line even in victory
protocol.Bloodname stake: A second loss discredits the name itself, not merely the forfeited machine

sidebarKernel.kernel: Why a Clan teaches by nearly killing: the logic of blooding green warriors against a chosen enemy, and what a Star Commander accepts as the cost of making warriors.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT — THE BENCHES
phases.lead: The Trial is won and lost on the rock bridges between the basalt benches. The green Star bloods itself in the first exchanges, and control of a central bridge decides whether it fights concentrated or is rolled up in detail.

dataBlock.Bridge control: Single-'Mech chokepoints; a bench can only be reinforced across a held bridge
dataBlock.Blooding curve: Each turn a green warrior survives in combat hardens their skill a step toward Regular
dataBlock.Fall hazard: A 'Mech pushed off a bench edge is lost to the ravine
dataBlock.Concentration deadline: Hold a central bridge by T+12:00 or be defeated bench by bench

sidebarKernel.kernel: Fighting on basalt benches over lava tubes: the piloting margins on a single-'Mech bridge, and why a knockdown here is not a recoverable mistake.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — THE GRIEVANCE SETTLED
phases.lead: The Trial reaches its formal decision and {NPC:opfor-commander} commits to the bench where the bloodname is decided. A clean win settles the line's honor; a survival that does not break the rival schedules the next grievance.

dataBlock.Single combat: Defeating {NPC:opfor-commander} personally settles the grievance beyond re-opening
dataBlock.Formal decision: The Trial resolves by convention at T+28:00; a Star without a decisive bench has lost
dataBlock.The blooded Star: Survivors emerge tested — the secondary objective measures cohesion, not casualty count

title: OPERATION SPITE EMBARGO
skeleton: relief force must break a punitive blockade that exists purely as spite for an earlier defiance, where destroying it too thoroughly provokes the besieger's withheld reserve and a weather-gated chokepoint meters every convoy against a starvation clock
inspiration: the Berlin Blockade and airlift, 1948 (a stranglehold imposed as political punishment, where the relief had to outlast the spite rather than win outright)
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, Periphery border, {YEAR}. A mining settlement refused to pay the protection tithe that a regional strongman, {NPC:opfor-commander}, demanded after his last raid was driven off. His answer was not another raid but a blockade: a stranglehold on the one road that feeds the settlement, set up purely to starve the town that humiliated him. {EMPLOYER}, the settlement's mining cooperative, has no C-bills and pays in refined ore. They have hired your command to break the blockade and reopen the road. They also know that breaking it cleanly will only provoke the strongman into squeezing harder. The terrain problem is the defile: a 4-kilometer canyon cut by a seasonal meltwater river. It is the only ground-vehicle route between the settlement and the railhead, where its ore is sold and its food is bought. {NPC:opfor-commander} has dug in a toll and blockade at the defile's narrows, where the canyon pinches to 30 meters. There, the river crossing forces traffic onto a ford that floods too deep to pass for 6 hours after any upland rain. {NPC:intel-source}, a teamster who runs the ore wagons and has been turned back at the toll three times, reports the blockade as one lance of worn 'Mechs plus a mix of tracked and wheeled armor scraped from the strongman's holdings, Green-to-Regular, dug in at the narrows with the high canyon walls covering the ford. That report is 7 days old. The settlement's problem is simple math: 19 days of food left at current rationing, and the ore that pays for resupply cannot move until the road opens. Break the blockade and the food moves. Fail and the town surrenders or starves. What the cooperative would rather not think about: {NPC:opfor-commander} has held back most of his strength, and crushing his blockade is exactly the humiliation that brings the rest of it down on the settlement. The 2,800 miners and their families live here and have nowhere else to go. If it comes to it, they will fight beside you with hunting rifles and mining charges. No help is coming but yours.

objectives.primary: Break {NPC:opfor-commander}'s blockade at the defile and reopen the road between the settlement and the railhead to ore and food traffic.
objectives.secondary: Get at least one ore convoy through to the railhead and one food convoy back before the settlement's 19-day reserve runs out.
objectives.bonus: Damage the blockade force badly enough that {NPC:opfor-commander} cannot quickly re-establish it, buying the settlement a real respite rather than a brief reopening.

complications.name: The Flooding Ford
complications.text: The ford floods to impassable depth for 6 hours after any upland rain, and the season makes rain a near-daily gamble. The flood blocks the road as surely as the blockade does, and it does not care which side it strands. Timing the convoy to the dry window is half the battle.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll 1d6 at the start of each operational day: on a 1-2 an upland rain has flooded the ford, closing it to all traffic for 6 hours and stranding any unit caught mid-crossing on the far bank.

complications.name: Payment in Ore
complications.text: The cooperative has no C-bills. It pays in refined ore, and that ore only becomes money once it is hauled to the railhead and sold. So any cash cost here is really a cost in ore the blockade is stopping them from selling. The contract pays only if the road opens.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any decision-point option with a C-bill cost is repriced as a deferred ore-payment lien against the reopened road; if the primary objective fails, the unit collects nothing, as the ore cannot move.

complications.name: The Strongman's Reserve
complications.text: {NPC:opfor-commander} has committed only part of his strength to the defile. A clean, humiliating defeat of the blockade is the provocation that brings the rest down on the settlement. Winning too well wins the battle and loses the town.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the blockade force is destroyed rather than driven off, the bonus objective inverts: the strongman commits his reserve and the resolution shifts toward the FAILURE-adjacent reprisal fork at elevated threat.

decisionPoints.name: Breaking the Narrows
decisionPoints.context: The blockade sits where the defile pinches to 30 meters with the ford under the canyon walls' guns. You can force the narrows head-on, find a way around the strongman's chosen ground, or break the blockade by cutting off what sustains it rather than fighting through it.

options.title: Force the Narrows Directly
advantages: Fastest reopening of the road if it succeeds
A 30-meter frontage limits how much the blockade can bring to bear at once
disadvantages: The canyon walls' guns cover the ford and the narrows is the strongman's prepared killing ground
A unit caught at the ford when it floods is trapped under those guns
options.consequence: You take the road by main force, paying in the canyon's prepared fires; the road opens fast or not at all.

costs.resource: casualties: a frontal push through the pinched ford under the wall guns is the bloodiest way through
costs.risk: A flood roll during the assault strands the lead element on the far bank under the blockade's prepared fire

options.title: Flank Over the Canyon Rim
advantages: A climb to the canyon rim takes the blockade's wall guns from above and behind
Bypasses the prepared ford killing ground entirely
disadvantages: The rim route is passable only to lighter 'Mechs and not to the convoy that must follow
A force divided between rim and floor can be defeated in detail if the timing slips
options.consequence: You unhinge the blockade from above but split your force to do it, and the convoy still has to come through the floor afterward.

costs.resource: engineering: scouting and marking a 'Mech-passable rim route before the assault
costs.risk: A force divided between rim and floor invites defeat in detail if the rim element arrives late or the floor element commits early

options.title: Cut the Blockade's Supply Line
advantages: A scratch blockade force fed from the strongman's holdings folds if its own resupply is severed
Avoids a direct fight at the prepared narrows
disadvantages: Strangling the blockade out takes days the settlement's food reserve may not have
Raiding the strongman's supply route is the kind of provocation that brings his reserve out early
options.consequence: You break the blockade by attrition rather than assault, trading the settlement's dwindling days for a fight avoided at the narrows.

costs.resource: time against the 19-day food reserve — a siege of the besiegers the town may not be able to wait out
costs.risk: Raiding his supply line provokes the strongman's reserve before the blockade has even folded

entries.event: Relief force enters the defile; the blockade's lookouts on the canyon rim signal the narrows and the dug-in force stands to.
Blockade wall guns open on the ford approach; the strongman's armor shifts to cover the narrows; a rim-flank element, if sent, begins its climb.
The narrows must be broken or unhinged by now to push a convoy through inside the day's dry window before a flood roll can close the ford.
If the blockade still holds, {NPC:opfor-commander} is alerted that his position is under serious attack and weighs committing his reserve from the holdings.
The strongman's reserve can reach the defile from this point; a blockade not yet broken becomes a two-sided fight the relief force cannot sustain.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The narrows must be broken and a convoy moving by T+16:00. Later than that, {NPC:opfor-commander} commits his reserve from the holdings. The relief force is then caught in the defile between the blockade and its reinforcements, with the road still shut and the settlement still starving.

opforSketch.composition: One lance of worn 'Mechs (30-55 tons, poorly maintained) at Green-to-Regular quality, supported by a scratch armor mix of 5 to 7 tracked and wheeled vehicles (Scorpion/Pegasus/Goblin behavior) dug in at the canyon narrows with the high walls covering the ford. A blockade, not a field force — emplaced, supply-dependent, holding ground it did not choose for a fight it would rather not have.
opforSketch.behavior: Blockade doctrine: hold the narrows and the ford guns, tax or turn back traffic, and avoid a decisive engagement that would consume a force the strongman cannot easily replace. The blockade fights hard from prepared positions but is brittle — it breaks contact and abandons the narrows at 35 percent force damage rather than be destroyed, falling back toward the strongman's holdings to be rebuilt.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN ROAD
forks.trigger: Blockade broken and damaged badly enough that it cannot quickly re-form; an ore convoy out and a food convoy in before the reserve runs out.
forks.consequence: The Reach breathes, and {NPC:opfor-commander}, his blockade wrecked and his reserve unwilling to throw good force after bad, sues for an uneasy truce — your command is retained to garrison the reopened road against the day he changes his mind.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND SQUEEZE
forks.trigger: Blockade driven off and the road reopened, but the strongman's strength is largely intact.
forks.consequence: Humiliated again, {NPC:opfor-commander} brings down the reserve he held back — a heavier blockade or a punitive raid that your command must now break a second time, the embargo escalated into open war over the road.

forks.name: OPERATION HUNGRY REACH
forks.trigger: Blockade holds, the relief force is mauled in the defile, or the food reserve runs out before the road opens.
forks.consequence: The settlement faces capitulation or starvation. {EMPLOYER} begs your command to cover an exodus of the settlement's families to a neighboring holding before the strongman's terms turn punitive — an escort of refugees down a road still under his guns.

storyElementSeed: A teamster sits with the relief commander on the dry stones above the ford. He points at the high-water mark stained on the canyon wall, well above a 'Mech's knee. The river, he explains, has killed more wagons than the strongman ever has, so the only schedule that matters here is the rain's.

merc.objectives.primary: Contract pays in refined ore against the road reopening — no road, no payout, and the ore is collateral you can only collect by succeeding. Break the blockade, move the convoys, and the lien clears at the railhead. Read the no-cash-escrow terms before you price a single option.

That adds two days of travel each way and pushes the slow strangle past the settlement's food reserve. The option works only if the settlement can stretch its rations further than the brief assumes.

phases.name: POSTURE — THE CLOSED ROAD
phases.lead: The relief force learns the defile before it fights for it — the ford's flood rhythm, the blockade's habits, and the settlement's shrinking larder. The road is the whole campaign in four kilometers of canyon.

dataBlock.Blockade: 1 worn 'Mech lance plus 5-7 scratch armor vehicles, dug in under the wall guns
dataBlock.Settlement clock: 19 days of food at current rationing; ore stockpile frozen until the road opens
dataBlock.Flood rhythm: Ford impassable 6 hours after any upland rain — a near-daily gamble this season

routes.name: BRINE — THE FORD APPROACH
routes.desc: The direct ground-vehicle road through the narrows and across the ford
routes.tradeoff: The only convoy-capable route; runs straight through the prepared killing ground under the wall guns

routes.name: SCREE — THE CANYON RIM
routes.desc: A 'Mech-only climb to the rim above the blockade
