title: OPERATION SWORN STATEMENT
skeleton: protectors must deliver a fragile witness across a single exposed span to give the testimony that names a reprisal's author, against a fanatical cell that will spend itself entirely for one shot and a deadline that convenes only once
inspiration: the witness-protection delivery against an organized contract to silence (the mob-trial pattern of a star witness who must reach the stand alive past a sworn effort to stop them)
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} core, {YEAR}. A Word of Blake reprisal cell razed a border town to punish a parliamentary vote that condemned the Blakist occupation. One witness can name the cell's commander to the Estates General: a surviving municipal records clerk, now sheltering in the provincial assembly town under your command's protection. {EMPLOYER}, a provincial deputy whose vote provoked the reprisal, needs the witness alive and on the assembly floor in 5 days. A named, sworn statement turns a deniable atrocity into a clear cause for war that the wavering provinces cannot ignore. The Blakist cell needs the witness dead before then, and has already tried once. The terrain problem is the causeway span, a 2-kilometer bridge carrying the only hard road from the assembly town's island core to the mainland district where the witness must testify. It crosses a tidal estuary a 'Mech cannot wade. The span is the witness's only route to the assembly floor, and the cell's best chance to kill the convoy carrying them. {NPC:intel-source}, a provincial intelligence liaison, reports the cell as one mixed 'Mech lance plus a strike team backed by hover armor and VTOLs, Veteran quality, willing to die to silence the witness. The liaison rates an all-out attempt on the span during the transit as very likely. That report is 3 days old and rated reliable. The witness is fragile: a records clerk, not a soldier, shaken by the razing and likely to bolt. Guarding the body is only half the task; steadying the nerves is the other half. What the deputy will not say on the assembly floor: the razing was itself an answer to his vote, and a sworn statement naming the cell is the next move in a chain. Win or lose, it will bring a heavier Blakist blow down on the province. The assembly town holds 90,000 residents, packed along the convoy route, and the cell will not hesitate to use them as cover or spend them as casualties. Five days to the testimony. The cell needs only one.

objectives.primary: Keep the witness alive and deliver them to the Estates General assembly floor in the provincial assembly town to give a sworn statement within the 5-day window.
objectives.secondary: Defeat or break the Blakist reprisal cell's attempt on the witness so decisively that they cannot mount a second try before the testimony is given.
objectives.bonus: Capture a member of the cell alive, producing corroborating testimony that makes the witness's statement unimpeachable before the wavering provinces.

complications.name: The Fragile Witness
complications.text: The witness is a records clerk, not a soldier, and the razing has left them prone to panic and flight. Protecting the body is only half the duty; a witness who bolts at the wrong moment, or refuses to cross the span, fails the mission as surely as a sniper would.
complications.mechanicalEffect: At each point of high stress — an attack on the convoy, a near-miss, the span crossing — roll 2d6: on 5 or less the witness panics, halting or scattering the protective formation for one turn unless a command unit is adjacent to steady them.

complications.name: The Crowded Route
complications.text: Ninety thousand residents pack the convoy route and the span approaches. The cell will use the crowd as cover for its strike team and as hostages against your fires. Every weapon discharged near the assembly town is a political act the deputy will answer for.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Hexes along the convoy route contain concealed civilian crowds; any area-effect fire or collateral damage in them imposes an immediate employer-standing penalty and voids the bonus objective, and the cell may place its strike team within crowd hexes until it fires.

complications.name: Fanatical Resolve
complications.text: The reprisal cell will spend itself entirely to silence the witness. They do not break at normal thresholds, do not retreat to preserve force, and will trade their whole strength for one clean shot at the convoy. Stopping them means stopping all of them.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The Blakist cell ignores morale and damage-threshold withdrawal entirely; units fight until destroyed or mission-failed, and any cell unit that reaches direct-fire range of the witness's transport gets a guaranteed attack before it can be neutralized.

decisionPoints.name: Crossing the Span
decisionPoints.context: The witness must cross the causeway span to reach the assembly floor, and the cell knows it. You can run the span fast and exposed, secure it methodically first, or deny the cell its target by moving the witness another way entirely.

options.title: Run the Span at Speed
advantages: A fast transit minimizes the window the cell has to strike on the bridge
Keeps the witness moving toward the deadline without delay
disadvantages: A convoy at speed on a 2-kilometer span has no cover and no room to maneuver if hit
A single disabled vehicle blocks the cantilever and traps everything behind it
options.consequence: You bet the crossing on speed and surprise; if the cell springs its strike mid-span, the convoy fights strung out on a bridge with the estuary on both sides.

costs.resource: exposure: a high-speed convoy crosses 2km of open cantilever with no cover and no fallback
costs.risk: One disabled vehicle on the span blocks the cantilever and the whole convoy is pinned over open water

options.title: Secure the Span First, Then Cross
advantages: Clearing the span and its approaches before the convoy moves denies the cell its prepared positions
Lets the protective force fight on its own terms rather than reacting on the bridge
disadvantages: A deliberate clearance burns hours against a 5-day clock the cell can stretch with feints
Securing the span signals exactly when and where the convoy will cross
options.consequence: You trade time and surprise for a cleared route; the cell, denied the span, may strike the staging area instead or wait for the testimony itself.

costs.resource: time: a deliberate span clearance spends a day of the five against a deadline the cell exploits
costs.risk: A telegraphed crossing lets the cell pick a different moment — the staging area or the assembly steps instead of the span

options.title: Move the Witness by Water Instead
advantages: A small boat across the estuary bypasses the span the cell has surely targeted
Splits the cell's attention if a decoy convoy still runs the bridge
disadvantages: The estuary crossing exposes the witness to the cell's VTOL support with no 'Mech cover on the water
A fragile witness on open water in a small craft is one panic away from disaster
options.consequence: You deny the cell its chosen ground at the cost of putting the witness somewhere your 'Mechs cannot protect them, trusting a decoy to draw the strike.

costs.resource: watercraft and a decoy convoy to sell the span crossing
costs.risk: The witness on open water is beyond your 'Mechs' reach — if the cell reads the feint, the VTOLs have an undefended target

entries.event: Convoy departs the assembly town island core for the span; cell observers in the crowd mark the movement and signal the strike team.
Convoy reaches the span approach; the cell's hover and VTOL elements move to interdict, the 'Mech lance positioning to block the far end.
The witness must be across the span and onto the mainland district road by now to reach the assembly floor inside the testimony window.
If the convoy is held short of the span or pinned on it, the cell commits its full strength to a decisive attempt before relief can arrive.
League security reinforcements from the assembly garrison can reach the span; a cell not yet broken makes its final fanatical push before they arrive.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The witness must be across the causeway span and clear of the bridge by T+9:00. Miss it and the cell pins the convoy on the open span, where your escort has no cover and no room, and presses its all-out attempt. Even if the witness lives, the testimony deadline is lost.

opforSketch.composition: One mixed Blakist reprisal 'Mech lance (40-70 tons) at Veteran quality, supported by a hover-armor section and VTOL gunships (2 to 4 rotary-wing) and a dismounted strike team that fights as narrative dressing among the crowds. Fielded to interdict a moving convoy on a fixed route. Fanatical, willing to spend the whole force for one clean shot at the witness.
opforSketch.behavior: Assassination-interdiction doctrine: the cell does not seek to win a battle but to reach and kill one target, accepting any loss to do it. The hover and VTOL elements probe for a gap while the 'Mech lance blocks the convoy's progress and channels it onto killing ground. The cell ignores damage-threshold withdrawal entirely and presses any unit that gets a line on the witness's transport, spending itself to the last machine.

forks.name: OPERATION NAMED HAND
forks.trigger: Witness delivers the sworn statement AND a cell member is captured alive to corroborate it, the atrocity proven beyond deniability.
forks.consequence: The testimony swings the wavering provinces and the Estates General authorizes a punitive expedition. {EMPLOYER}, his vote vindicated, secures your command the lead in the follow-on raid to seize the named Blakist cell's forward base before it can disperse.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND CELL
forks.trigger: Witness delivered and the statement given, the reprisal cell broken, but no captive secured.
forks.consequence: The statement lands but the Blakist command answers the casus belli with a heavier reprisal cell sent to silence the deputy himself. Your command shifts to securing {EMPLOYER} and the assembly against the next, larger attempt.

forks.name: OPERATION SILENCED CLERK
forks.trigger: Witness killed, the testimony deadline missed, or the convoy destroyed on the span.
forks.consequence: With the witness silenced, the atrocity stays deniable and the Blakists ascendant. {EMPLOYER}, exposed and desperate, pulls your command into a covering action as the province's loyalist holdouts withdraw ahead of the reprisal the failed testimony failed to prevent.

storyElementSeed: The records clerk grips the transport door handle at the foot of the causeway span, staring down two kilometers of empty bridge with the estuary glittering on both sides. The section commander has thirty seconds to decide whether to talk them across or carry them. The assembly floor will not convene twice, and the deadline will not move.

comstar.situation: {WORLD}, {YEAR}. A schismatic cell of our own order has answered a parliamentary condemnation with fire, razing a provincial town as reprisal, and the single witness who can name its commander to the Estates General shelters under your protection in the assembly town. The witness must reach the assembly floor across the causeway span in five days; the cell needs only the one crossing to silence them. The Word that razed the town will answer a sworn naming with a heavier hand — information here is both shield and provocation.

merc.objectives.primary: Contract is body-and-delivery: the witness alive on the assembly floor within 5 days, full payout, no partial credit for a live witness who never testifies. The political fallout is the deputy's problem; the clerk in one piece on the floor is yours. Section 4 prices the failure clause — read it.

title: OPERATION KNOWN QUANTITY
skeleton: recon element must determine whether a massed reprisal force is the feared veteran formation or a feint wearing borrowed banners, from a finite set of one-use silhouette positions, where being seen scouting is itself the intelligence that decides how the enemy commits
inspiration: the pre-Kursk reconnaissance problem, 1943 (confirming whether a massed force was the real main effort or a deception, where the act of looking risked revealing one's own uncertainty)
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, contested HPG world, {YEAR}. {TARGET_FACTION} has massed a reprisal force in the highlands to answer a raid that cost them a relay station. {EMPLOYER}'s whole response hinges on one question that orbit cannot answer: is this the feared veteran formation its banners claim, or a hasty feint meant to pull {EMPLOYER}'s reserve out of position before the real blow lands somewhere else? Your command is to confirm the force's true makeup and quality up close, then withdraw with the answer before the reprisal moves. The prize is certainty, not ground. The terrain problem is the highland pass: folded ridgelines above the plateau where the enemy is staging. You can see the staging ground from only three overwatch knobs, each a bare rock outcrop with one covered approach and no second way off. A recon 'Mech on a knob can see the staging ground, but it stands exposed against the sky. Once a knob has been used and spotted, it cannot be used safely again. {NPC:intel-source}, a Precentor's deep-cover agent inside the {TARGET_FACTION} supply train, puts the staging force at battalion strength by its banners, but cannot tell whether the 'Mechs behind those banners are first-line machines or a scratch collection wearing borrowed paint. That report is 2 days old, and the source cannot get closer without being caught. The difference decides everything. A real veteran reprisal needs {EMPLOYER}'s full reserve; committing that reserve against a feint leaves the true target undefended. The brief states the danger plainly: the enemy runs its own recon screen, and if it spots your scouts on the knobs, it learns that {EMPLOYER} is unsure. That doubt is itself intelligence, and it shapes how the enemy commits. Looking risks telling them you needed to look. The plateau is war-scarred, its towns long emptied by repeated battles over the HPG compound. Only the ridges, the staging ground, and two recon screens remain, each trying not to be the first one seen.

objectives.primary: Confirm the true composition and quality of the {TARGET_FACTION} reprisal force in the highlands — veteran first-line or scratch feint — and withdraw with the verified answer.
objectives.secondary: Complete the reconnaissance without being detected, so the enemy does not learn that {EMPLOYER}'s response hinges on uncertainty.
objectives.bonus: Identify the reprisal force's intended objective from its staging dispositions, revealing not only what it is but where it means to strike.

complications.name: The Silhouette Knobs
complications.text: The three overwatch knobs are the only positions that see the staging ground, and each one silhouettes whatever stands on it. A knob once occupied and spotted is burned — the enemy screen watches it thereafter. There are three looks available and no more.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each of the three knobs may be occupied once; occupying a knob grants one composition-assessment roll but risks detection (2d6, detected on 5 or less, modified by movement and time spent). A detected knob cannot be re-used and raises the detection difficulty on the remaining knobs.

complications.name: Banners Can Lie
complications.text: The reprisal force flies the banners of a feared veteran formation, but banners are only paint. The 'Mechs behind them may be first-line, or a scratch collection borrowing the colors to look scarier. Counting machines is not enough. You have to judge their quality from how they move, maintain, and screen.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A single overwatch look yields machine count and banner identity only; determining true quality (veteran versus scratch) requires either a second corroborating look from a different knob or a close-approach assessment that sharply raises detection risk.

complications.name: Being Seen Reveals Your Doubt
complications.text: If the enemy spots your scouts on the knobs, it learns that {EMPLOYER} is unsure enough to send them. That doubt is intelligence the enemy uses to decide how to commit. So being seen costs you more than the recon force. It also gives away that your side is still guessing.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the recon force is detected, the SUCCESS and FULL_SUCCESS forks are unavailable regardless of whether the composition was confirmed; the enemy adjusts its commitment to {EMPLOYER}'s revealed uncertainty and the resolution shifts toward the COMPROMISED branch.

decisionPoints.name: Reading the Force
decisionPoints.context: Three knobs, three looks, and a question that may need more than one of them to answer. You can confirm composition from distance across multiple knobs, close to confirm quality at higher risk, or hold one knob in reserve against the enemy's own screen — each weighs certainty against exposure.

options.title: Distance Assessment Across the Knobs
advantages: Multiple long looks cross-check the count and quality without ever closing the range
Keeps the recon force out of the enemy screen's effective reach
disadvantages: Distance reads quality poorly — banners and machine counts, not crew skill
Using all three knobs to be sure leaves no look in reserve if one read is ambiguous
options.consequence: You build certainty by accumulation, spending your looks to cross-check; if the reads disagree, there is no fourth knob to break the tie.

costs.resource: looks: cross-checking from distance spends multiple of the three available knobs
costs.risk: Distance cannot confirm crew quality — you may leave certain of the count and guessing at the threat

options.title: Close to Confirm Quality
advantages: A close approach reads maintenance, drill, and screen discipline — the true marks of quality
One good close look can answer the whole question definitively
disadvantages: Closing the range puts the recon force inside the enemy screen's detection envelope
A detected close approach forfeits the secret and may not survive to report
options.consequence: You go for the definitive answer at the highest exposure; success ends all doubt, detection ends the mission's deniability and possibly the recon force.

costs.resource: exposure: a close approach enters the enemy reconnaissance screen's effective range
costs.risk: Detection inside the screen forfeits the secret that {EMPLOYER} was uncertain and may cost the recon force its withdrawal

options.title: Hold a Knob Against the Enemy Screen
advantages: Keeping one knob in reserve lets the recon force watch for the enemy's own scouts
Detecting the enemy screen first preserves the option of clean withdrawal
disadvantages: A knob spent watching the screen is a knob not spent reading the force
Caution may yield a confident answer about the screen and an incomplete one about the force
options.consequence: You buy security against being seen at the cost of a look at the thing you came to see; the answer may be partial but the withdrawal stays clean.

costs.resource: intelligence yield: a knob spent on counter-recon is a look not spent on the staging force
costs.risk: A partial answer about the reprisal force may force {EMPLOYER} to decide on incomplete data anyway

entries.event: Recon force reaches the first overwatch knob's covered approach; the enemy reconnaissance screen is active across the staging ground's ridgelines.
First overwatch look taken; the detection roll resolves and the recon force decides whether to shift knobs, close, or withdraw on the partial read.
A confirmed composition assessment must be in hand by now to withdraw before the reprisal force completes its own staging and begins to move.
If the recon force is still on the knobs, the enemy screen's sweep pattern reaches the occupied prominences and detection becomes near-certain.
The reprisal force completes staging and commits; a recon force that has not withdrawn with its answer is caught between the screen and the moving column.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: You must have a verified assessment and be pulling the recon force out by T+11:00. Miss it and the enemy screen's sweep catches your scouts on the knobs at T+17:00, and the reprisal force commits at T+24:00 with {EMPLOYER} still blind to what it faces.

opforSketch.composition: A staging reprisal force at battalion banner strength — but its true nature is the mission's question: either first-line 'Mechs (mixed weights, 35-85 tons) at Veteran quality, or a scratch collection (worn light and medium machines, 30-55 tons) at Green-to-Regular quality wearing borrowed colors. Backed by a dedicated reconnaissance screen of fast light 'Mechs patrolling the ridgelines. No combat vehicles on the recon-encounter board — if contact occurs it is a fast-'Mech screen action, scout against scout.
opforSketch.behavior: Screen doctrine: the enemy reconnaissance element patrols the overwatch approaches to deny observation of the staging ground and to detect any scouting attempt — because a detected enemy scout tells them their opponent is uncertain. The screen does not seek a stand-up fight; it seeks contact long enough to identify and report, then breaks to carry the warning. It pursues a detected recon force only far enough to confirm its presence, not to destroy it.

forks.name: OPERATION FULL ANSWER
forks.trigger: Composition and quality confirmed, the recon force undetected, AND the reprisal force's intended objective identified from its dispositions.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} knows exactly what it faces and where it will fall. Forewarned, the order positions its reserve precisely and tasks your command to lead the spoiling raid that pre-empts the reprisal at its staging ground before it can launch.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAR EYES
forks.trigger: Composition and quality confirmed and the recon force withdrawn undetected, the reprisal's objective still unknown.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} knows the force's true weight and commits the right reserve to meet it. Your command, the unit that read the threat true, is held as the reserve's spearhead for the garrison defense the confirmed reprisal will fall upon.

forks.name: OPERATION BLIND COMMIT
forks.trigger: Recon force detected, or the composition left unconfirmed.
forks.consequence: Detected, the recon force has told the enemy that {EMPLOYER} is uncertain, and the reprisal commits to exploit that doubt — striking where the reserve is not. Your command races to cover the exposed real target, fighting the reprisal on the worst possible terms.

storyElementSeed: A scout on the second knob holds her 'Mech dead still on the bare rock, watching the staging ground through a magnification scope. She counts not machines but the small signs that give away a unit's quality: the spacing of the pickets, the discipline of the fuel line, the way the maintenance crews move. Whether she reads it right will decide where an entire reserve goes.

merc.objectives.primary: Contract is a verified intelligence product, paid on delivery of a confirmed assessment: is the staging force first-line or a paint job. A guess does not pay; a sourced, cross-checked answer does. The order's auditors will weigh the confidence, not the effort — read the deliverable clause before you spend a look.

clan.situation: {WORLD}, {YEAR}. A force has massed in the highlands to answer a raid, flying the banners of a feared formation. You are to learn whether those banners cover true warriors or a feint of lesser machines wearing borrowed honor, and to withdraw with the truth unseen. The three overwatch knobs above the plateau give the only view of the staging ground. Each stands the watcher against the sky, and each may be used only once. If the enemy sees you scouting, he learns you are unsure, and that doubt becomes a weapon in his hand.

title: OPERATION ROOT AND BRANCH
skeleton: assault must take an elevated plateau by one of four prepared ramps to end a reprisal chain at its source, capturing the infrastructure intact while a cornered garrison's last reflex is to scorch the very prize and the civilians beneath it
inspiration: the assault on the Vercors plateau / Monte Cassino's approach roads (taking dominating high ground by a handful of prepared ascents against a defender who would rather destroy than yield)
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, periphery march, {YEAR}. This is where the chain began. A {TARGET_FACTION} garrison launched the raid that started the reprisal cycle your command has fought across three systems. {EMPLOYER}, an SLDF division command worn down by trading blow for blow, means to end it at the source: take the world and strip the garrison of its power to raid. Your command leads the assault landing. The terrain problem is the tablelands, a single raised plateau 60 kilometers across. It holds the garrison's DropPort, its 'Mech bays, and the fusion plant that powers both. From the lowland landing zones, only four graded ramp roads climb the tableland's basalt rim. The garrison holds the high ground, the ramps, and the time to wire them for demolition. {NPC:intel-source}, an SLDF Intelligence Command cell that has tracked this garrison across the whole reprisal chain, reports the defenders as a reinforced battalion: mixed 'Mechs and a strong armor regiment, Regular-to-Veteran quality. All four rim ramps are wired to blow, and the garrison commander, {NPC:opfor-commander}, holds a mobile reserve to counter whichever ramp you commit to. That report is 4 days old and rated reliable. The purpose shapes the plan. {EMPLOYER} wants the garrison's raiding power destroyed: its 'Mech bays, its DropPort, its reach off-world. But the plateau also holds the world's only fusion plant and the 40,000 civilians in the DropPort township who depend on it. Ending the raids by burning the world down is an outcome {EMPLOYER}'s conscience will not allow. The brief does not soften the danger: a garrison about to lose its world may lash out one last time, wrecking the plant in a scorched withdrawal and poisoning the victory. Taking the source of the chain may force its worst link. The 40,000 in the township have lived under this garrison for a generation, and the SLDF will not trade their survival for a clean military result. The order is to end it. The brief cannot promise the ending will be clean.

objectives.primary: Seize the tablelands and destroy the {TARGET_FACTION} garrison's raiding capacity — its 'Mech bays and DropPort facilities — ending its ability to project force off-world.
objectives.secondary: Capture the tableland's fusion plant intact and prevent a scorched-earth demolition, preserving the 40,000 civilians of the DropPort township who depend on it.
objectives.bonus: Capture {NPC:opfor-commander} and the garrison's mobile reserve intact, decapitating the reprisal chain rather than merely breaking it and denying the source a martyr.

complications.name: The Four Ramps
complications.text: Only four graded ramp roads climb the tableland's basalt rim, and the garrison has wired all four for demolition. A blown ramp denies the assault that approach but commits the garrison's prepared charges; an unblown ramp the garrison is saving is one it means to counter-attack down. Which ramp you take is the whole battle's hinge.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each of the four ramps may be demolished by the defender once committed against it; a demolished ramp is impassable to 'Mechs for the remainder of the engagement, and the defender's mobile reserve deploys to counter the ramp the assault commits its main weight to.

complications.name: The Plant and the Township
complications.text: The fusion plant powers the garrison and the 40,000-soul township alike, and it sits at the heart of the tableland. The garrison may demolish it as a final reprisal; the assault must not destroy it in the taking. A military victory that darkens the township is the outcome the order forbids.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the fusion plant is destroyed — by defender demolition or assault collateral fire — the secondary objective fails permanently and the resolution shifts toward the FAILURE-adjacent fork regardless of whether the garrison is defeated.

complications.name: A Garrison With Nothing to Lose
complications.text: A garrison about to lose its world may spend its last strength on a final reprisal rather than a withdrawal — the plant demolished, the bays cratered, the township punished for sheltering the SLDF. Ending the chain at its source may force its worst link, and a cornered {NPC:opfor-commander} is the most dangerous he has ever been.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Once the garrison drops below 40 percent effective strength, the gamemaster rolls each turn for a scorched-withdrawal trigger; if triggered, the defender shifts all remaining effort to demolition objectives (plant, bays, DropPort) rather than defense, racing the assault to ruin what it cannot hold.

decisionPoints.name: Committing the Assault
decisionPoints.context: The garrison holds the high ground and a reserve poised to counter your chosen ramp. You can mass against one ramp and accept its prepared defenses, feint at one and assault another, or split the assault to take two ramps at once — each commits the garrison's charges and reserve differently and risks the plant differently.

options.title: Mass Against One Ramp
advantages: Concentrated force gives the best chance of forcing a single ramp quickly
A fast lodgement on the tableland gets units to the plant before it can be wired
disadvantages: The garrison commits its full reserve and its prepared charges against the obvious main effort
A blown ramp under the massed assault funnels the whole force into a kill zone
options.consequence: You bet the assault on overwhelming one approach; if the ramp holds or blows, the concentrated force has no second axis to exploit.

costs.resource: casualties: a massed assault up a single prepared ramp pays the full price of the garrison's concentrated defense
costs.risk: The garrison blows the ramp under your main weight and the assault is funneled into prepared fires with no alternate axis

options.title: Feint One Ramp, Assault Another
advantages: Drawing the garrison's reserve and charges to a feint clears the real assault's path
A well-sold feint can take a ramp the garrison was saving for its own counter-attack
disadvantages: The feint force is exposed and may be destroyed selling the deception
If the garrison reads the feint, both the deception and the real assault arrive piecemeal
options.consequence: You trade a force to deceive the garrison's commitment; success unhinges the defense, failure spends the feint for nothing and warns the defender.

costs.resource: force committed: a feint force exposed to draw the garrison's reserve and charges
costs.risk: A garrison that reads the feint commits correctly and both efforts hit prepared defenses understrength

options.title: Split the Assault Across Two Ramps
advantages: Two simultaneous axes force the garrison to divide its reserve and its attention
If one ramp blows, the other axis still carries the assault onto the tableland
disadvantages: Neither axis is strong enough to force its ramp alone against a concentrated defense
Coordinating two assaults up separate ramps under demolition risk is its own battle
options.consequence: You hedge against a blown ramp by attacking two, accepting that each axis fights understrength and the garrison may yet mass against one and hold both.

costs.resource: coordination overhead: two simultaneous ramp assaults straining command across the basalt rim
costs.risk: The garrison concentrates against one axis, holds it, and the divided assault lacks the weight to force either ramp

entries.event: Assault landing complete in the lowland landing zones; the garrison's rim observers report the SLDF deployment and {NPC:opfor-commander} stands his battalion to.
Assault columns reach the rim ramps; the garrison's mobile reserve shifts toward the assault's apparent main effort and demolition teams stand ready at the ramps.
A lodgement on the tableland must be secured by now to reach the fusion plant before the garrison can complete its wiring for a scorched withdrawal.
If the garrison's effective strength has been driven below 40 percent, the scorched-withdrawal trigger becomes live and demolition of the plant and bays may begin.
The garrison's last organized resistance ends; whatever has been demolished by this point — plant, bays, DropPort — is the chain's final, irreversible reprisal.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: You must secure a foothold on the tableland and have a force moving on the fusion plant by T+14:00. Miss it and the cornered garrison finishes wiring its charges and answers the loss of its world with a scorched withdrawal. The plant and the township's power are destroyed, the chain's worst link, even as the garrison itself falls.

opforSketch.composition: A reinforced defending battalion: a mixed 'Mech force (35-85 tons across all weight classes) at Regular-to-Veteran quality and a strong armor regiment of tracked and wheeled vehicles (Manticore/Demolisher/Po behavior) holding the tableland's high ground and the four prepared ramps, with {NPC:opfor-commander}'s mobile reserve held to counter the assault's main axis. Prepared, dug in, holding home ground with demolition charges sited on every approach and on the plant itself.
opforSketch.behavior: Plateau-defense doctrine giving way to scorched reprisal: the garrison fights to hold the rim ramps and counter-attack the assault's main effort with its mobile reserve, trading ramps for time. As the defense fails, {NPC:opfor-commander}'s doctrine shifts from holding the world to denying it — below 40 percent strength the garrison abandons defensive cohesion to race the assault to demolition, spending its last force to ruin the plant, the bays, and the DropPort rather than yield them intact.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN ROOT
forks.trigger: Garrison's raiding capacity destroyed, the fusion plant captured intact, AND {NPC:opfor-commander} and the mobile reserve taken alive — the chain decapitated without a martyr.
forks.consequence: The reprisal cycle ends at its source, the township spared and the garrison's leadership in SLDF hands. {EMPLOYER} tasks your command with the cadre duty of standing up a loyal garrison on the pacified world — the chain converted from war into occupation.

forks.name: OPERATION HELD GROUND
forks.trigger: Tableland seized and the raiding capacity destroyed, the plant and township preserved, but {NPC:opfor-commander} or a fragment of the reserve escapes off-world.
forks.consequence: The world is taken and its raids ended, but the escaped commander carries the grievance off-world to begin anew. Your command garrisons the won tableland against the remnant's inevitable return — the chain broken here but not yet everywhere.

forks.name: OPERATION SCORCHED CROWN
forks.trigger: Assault fails, the fusion plant is destroyed, or the garrison completes its scorched withdrawal.
forks.consequence: The garrison answers its defeat by darkening the world — the plant demolished, the township's power gone, the victory poisoned. {EMPLOYER} commits your command to a desperate relief effort for the 40,000 civilians the failed assault could not protect, the chain's worst link forged at its end.

storyElementSeed: An assault company commander halts his lance at the foot of the third ramp, looking up sixty meters of graded basalt at the demolition charges he can see set into the rock face. He weighs the order to take the tableland against the plant lights still burning in the township below. He knows the garrison can put those lights out faster than he can climb.

is-davion.objectives.primary: End the raids by taking the base they fly from: bays cratered, DropPort wrecked, the garrison's reach broken. The plant stays standing and the township stays lit. We do not win a world by killing it. Taking the tableland is the harder job, but sparing the plant matters more.

clan.situation: {WORLD}, {YEAR}. This world launched the raid that began a cycle of reprisal, and {EMPLOYER} has resolved to end the matter at its root by taking the world and unmaking the garrison's capacity to raid. The tablelands hold the DropPort, the 'Mech bays, and the fusion plant, reachable from the lowlands by only four basalt ramp roads. To reduce the plateau by fire is to destroy the prize and the 40,000 who live beneath it; a clean conquest demands the high ground taken intact, the surat commander {NPC:opfor-commander} answered, and the world held rather than ruined.

phases.name: INGRESS — THE RIM RAMPS
phases.lead: The assault lands in the lowlands and must climb the basalt rim by one of four prepared ramps to reach the tableland the garrison holds. The choice of ramp commits the garrison's charges and its reserve.

dataBlock.The tableland: 60km elevated plateau holding the DropPort, 'Mech bays, and fusion plant
dataBlock.The ramps: Four graded basalt roads, all wired for demolition, the only 'Mech approaches
dataBlock.The garrison: Reinforced battalion plus armor regiment, Regular-to-Veteran, mobile reserve held back
dataBlock.Lodgement deadline: On the tableland and moving on the plant by T+14:00

routes.name: IRON — THE NORTH RAMP
routes.desc: The widest graded ramp, the obvious main-effort approach
routes.tradeoff: Best capacity for a massed assault; the ramp the garrison most expects and most heavily prepared

routes.name: EMBER — THE EAST RAMP
routes.desc: A narrower ramp nearer the fusion plant
routes.tradeoff: Quickest line to the plant once forced; tight enough that a demolition seals it for good

phases.protocol: Conscience-of-fire discipline binds the assault: the fusion plant and the township are protected ground, and no indirect or area fire is authorized within their arc. Codeword GREEN LIGHTS on the assault net means the plant is confirmed intact and the priority is its capture before demolition; SCORCHED, if heard, means the garrison's demolition has begun and the assault races to reach the plant before the charges fire.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Assaulting a prepared ramp wired to blow: reading seated demolition charges from the foot of a basalt rim, and the margin between climbing fast and climbing into a crater.

phases.name: GROUND — THE TABLELAND
phases.lead: On the plateau the assault must destroy the garrison's raiding capacity while sparing the plant the garrison would rather destroy than yield. A cornered commander's doctrine shifts from defense to denial.

dataBlock.Objectives on the plateau: 'Mech bays and DropPort to be wrecked; fusion plant to be taken intact
dataBlock.Reserve counter: {NPC:opfor-commander}'s mobile reserve counters the assault's committed axis
dataBlock.Scorch trigger: Below 40 percent garrison strength, demolition of plant and bays becomes live
dataBlock.Plant protection: Any fire that destroys the plant fails the secondary and the township with it

sidebarKernel.kernel: When a defender stops defending and starts destroying: reading the shift from holding ground to scorching it, and the assault tempo needed to reach the plant before a cornered garrison ruins it.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — THE WORLD HELD OR RUINED
phases.lead: The garrison's last resistance ends, but what survives the ending — the plant, the township's power, the commander himself — decides whether the chain is broken clean or forged one link worse at its very source.

dataBlock.Raiding capacity: Bays and DropPort confirmed destroyed — the garrison's reach ended
dataBlock.Plant and township: A plant intact and the township lit is the clean result; its loss poisons the win
dataBlock.Decapitation: {NPC:opfor-commander} and the reserve taken alive deny the chain a martyr and a remnant

sidebarKernel.kernel: Ending a reprisal chain at its root: why capturing the source's commander matters more than killing him, and how a martyr or an escaped remnant re-forges a chain you thought you had broken.
